Specifies extracting and trimming the reference, decoding valid application/c2pa base64 data: URIs (otherwise reporting manifest.appendOnlyText.noSentinel) and resolving other URIs per Section 14.5.3, reporting manifest.inaccessible if retrieval fails. The located store is that of the active checkpoint, with earlier checkpoints found by following the chain described in Section 14.12.6.

Requires the C2PA Manifest Store for unstructured text to be located using the procedure in Section A.8, Embedding Manifests into Unstructured Text. Requires the asset to be treated as if no manifests were located if no valid C2PATextManifestWrapper, or more than one, is found.
Requires the C2PA Manifest Store for TIFF-based assets to be located in either the first IFD or the last IFD.

Requires the C2PA Manifest Store for WARC files to be located per Section A.10 by scanning for a record with WARC-Type c2pa-provenance and Content-Type application/c2pa. Specifies that if none is found the file has no manifest store, if more than one is present the asset shall be treated as if no manifests were located, and if exactly one is found the store shall be extracted from its block. Notes that a companion CDX or CDXJ index may be used to locate the record without scanning the whole file.
Heading that opens section 14.5.3 By Reference or URI; it carries no text of its own.

Recommends that, when no store is embedded, a validator attempt in order to locate a remote C2PA Manifest Store via an HTTP Link header, an XMP dcterms:provenance URI, a font C2PA table with non-zero activeManifestUriLength, sidecar files named with an added or replacement .c2pa extension, or a similarly named entry in the same archive, stopping at the first found. Permits looking in other places if these fail. Requires the manifest.inaccessible error code when a documented remote manifest is missing or unreachable, and rejection with manifest.inaccessible.encrypted or manifest.inaccessible.malformed when a retrieved store is unreadable due to encryption or cannot be interpreted as valid.

Recommends that, for assets retrieved over HTTP, a validator look for a Link header (per RFC 8288) with rel=c2pa-manifest, from whose http or https URI the C2PA Manifest Store can be retrieved. Describes that the link may also refer to an embedded store using a JUMBF URI fragment to the C2PA Manifest Store superbox, and requires validators to ignore any childlabel portion since references to specific manifests are not permitted. Notes that HTTP refers to the protocol in RFC 9110, not only the http:// scheme.

Requires a validator to decompress compressed standard or update manifests before standard validation. Requires rejection with manifest.compressed.invalid if decompression fails or the brob box data is not a standard or update manifest.

Describes that a validator may wish to confirm that the located C2PA Manifest Store belongs to the asset. Requires using the active manifest's hard binding assertion for this, and, since a mismatch could mean either modification or the wrong store, requires treating it as a non-matching hard binding and rejecting with assertion.dataHash.mismatch, assertion.boxesHash.mismatch, assertion.collectionHash.mismatch, assertion.segmentHash.mismatch or assertion.bmffHash.mismatch depending on the assertion type.
Heading that opens section 14.6 Locating and Validating the Claim; it carries no text of its own.

Specifies locating the claim within the current manifest as the JUMBF superbox labelled c2pa.claim.v2 (or c2pa.claim for older claims) with JUMBF type UUID 6332636C-0011-0010-8000-00AA00389B71 (c2cl), which is the same for both formats. Requires exactly one such box, rejecting the manifest with claim.multiple if more than one is found.

Requires a claim whose content is not well-formed CBOR to be rejected with claim.cbor.invalid. Requires a c2pa.claim.v2 to contain instanceID, signature, created_assertions and claim_generator_info, and requires rejection with claim.malformed if any is missing or if claim_generator_info lacks a name field. Requires any icon field in the generator-info-map to be validated as described in Section 14.10.4.3, Validation of References.

Requires the validator to resolve the claim's signature field to the COSE signature, rejecting with claimSignature.missing if it is absent, unresolvable or outside the same C2PA Manifest box. Requires credential validation per Chapter 13, rejecting with signingCredential.invalid for unacceptable credentials and algorithm.unsupported for algorithms not on the allowed or deprecated lists. Requires checking for a valid time stamp first, then recommends verifying a chain of trust to a trust anchor configuration while honouring notBefore and notAfter, assigning signingCredential.trusted or rejecting with signingCredential.untrusted. Requires then verifying the signature per Section 12.3, assigning claimSignature.validated or rejecting with claimSignature.mismatch, and states that headers in the rest of the chapter mean the union of protected and unprotected headers.
Heading that opens section 14.8 Validate the Time Stamp; it carries no text of its own.
Heading that opens section 14.8.1 Obtaining the TimeStampToken; it carries no text of its own.

Specifies that when a sigTst or sigTst2 header is present its tstTokens array is expected to hold a single tstToken, and requires issuing timeStamp.malformed and ignoring the time stamps if there is more than one. Requires a validator supporting sigTst to take the val property as an RFC 3161 TimeStampResp, issue timeStamp.malformed and ignore it if the PKIStatusInfo status is not 0 (granted) or 1 (grantedWithMods), and otherwise use its timeStampToken. Requires a validator for sigTst2 to take the val property as an RFC 3161 timeStampToken.

Requires a validator to skip this step if a TimeStampToken from a sigTst or sigTst2 header has already passed validation, and to follow it otherwise. Requires that, if time stamp assertions were previously mapped from C2PA Manifest identifiers to TimeStampTokens, the validator use the token mapped to the current manifest's identifier, trying each one if several exist until one passes. States that no error is raised when the identifier is absent from the mapping.

Requires validators to check the timeStampToken's signature algorithm, signature, messageImprint presence, imprint hash algorithm, imprint match against the claim (sigTst) or COSE signature field (sigTst2), TSA certificate trust chain, and that genTime falls within the TSA and CA certificates' validity, issuing informational codes such as timeStamp.untrusted, timeStamp.mismatch, timeStamp.malformed or timeStamp.outsideValidity and ignoring the time stamp on failure. Requires issuing timeStamp.trusted and timeStamp.validated when all checks pass, then checking genTime against the claim signing certificate chain to return claimSignature.insideValidity or reject with claimSignature.outsideValidity. Notes that a failed time stamp does not by itself reject the manifest, that time stamps stay valid after the TSA credential expires, and that TSA revocation status is not required. Requires validators to use the attested time when a trusted, validated time stamp is present, and otherwise to use the current time to return claimSignature.insideValidity or reject with claimSignature.outsideValidity.

Permits a validator to check that the claimed time of signing in the iat protected header falls within the validity period of the signer's certificate and CA certificates and is no later than any trusted time stamp. Requires that a validator performing this check return the informational code timeOfSigning.insideValidity or timeOfSigning.outsideValidity accordingly.

Describes determining the revocation status of the signer's certificate and CA certificates in the trust chain as important to deciding validity and trust. Recommends determining CA certificate status via the AIA extension and any included OCSP responses, and requires rejection with signingCredential.untrusted if a CA certificate was revoked at the trusted time stamp time or current time. For the signer's certificate, requires treating it as not revoked when revocation status is unsupported, and validating stapled rVals OCSP responses and any certificate status assertions in other manifests per Section 14.9.1, trying each until one passes. Recommends that an online validator query the OCSP responder per Section 14.9.2 if no revocation information is found in the C2PA Manifest Store.

Requires a validator to decode OCSP responses per RFC 6960, including requirements 1 through 4 of section 3.2. Specifies that an accepted response establishes the certificate was not revoked at signing when the claim signature has a valid time stamp, a SingleResponse has status good with the current time no earlier than thisUpdate and the attested time before thisUpdate or within the (thisUpdate,nextUpdate) or (thisUpdate,producedAt + 24 hours) interval, and the signer is an authorized responder. Requires the validator then to issue signingCredential.ocsp.notRevoked or perform an online OCSP check, and to reject with signingCredential.ocsp.revoked if a response meets all conditions except that certStatus is revoked.

Permits a validator to query the OCSP responder online when no stored response satisfies Section 14.9.1 or the claim signature lacks a time stamp, noting that such queries can reveal the asset being validated. Requires signingCredential.ocsp.skipped if the check is not performed and signingCredential.ocsp.inaccessible if no response is received. Specifies that an accepted response establishes non-revocation when the time stamp time (or current time if no valid time stamp) falls within (thisUpdate,nextUpdate), certStatus is good or revoked with removeFromCRL, and the signer is an authorized responder, or when a revoked status with another reason has a revocationTime after a valid attested time stamp falling within that interval. Requires signingCredential.ocsp.notRevoked in those cases, otherwise signingCredential.ocsp.unknown for an unknown status or rejection with signingCredential.ocsp.revoked.
Heading that opens section 14.10 Validate the Assertions; it carries no text of its own.
Heading that opens section 14.10.1 Validate the correct assertions for the type of manifest; it carries no text of its own.
States that, depending on the type of manifest, some assertions are required or forbidden, and requires a validator to check for required and not-permitted assertions.

Specifies the assertion checks for a standard manifest: there shall be exactly one hard binding assertion (c2pa.hash.data, c2pa.hash.boxes, c2pa.hash.collection.data, c2pa.hash.segment, the deprecated c2pa.hash.bmff.v2, or c2pa.hash.bmff.v3), otherwise rejection with claim.hardBindings.missing or assertion.multipleHardBindings. It also requires at most one c2pa.ingredient assertion with relationship parentOf (else manifest.multipleParents) and at least one actions assertion in created_assertions or gathered_assertions (else claim.actions.missing). Finally, a c2pa.created or c2pa.opened action must appear in the first actions assertion of exactly one of those two lists, else the manifest is rejected with assertion.action.malformed.

Specifies the assertion checks for an update manifest: exactly one ingredient assertion with relationship parentOf must be present, otherwise rejection with manifest.update.wrongParents. The manifest shall be rejected with manifest.update.invalid if it contains any hard binding assertions (c2pa.hash.data, c2pa.hash.boxes, c2pa.hash.collection.data, c2pa.hash.segment, c2pa.hash.bmff.v2, c2pa.hash.bmff.v3), thumbnail assertions, or c2pa.hash.multi-asset assertions. Any action in c2pa.actions or c2pa.actions.v2 assertions must use one of the values supported for update manifests, else the same failure code applies.

Requires a validator processing a claim to gather the set of redacted assertions for each ingredient's manifest from the JUMBF URIs in its redacted_assertions field, and forbids a claim's redacted_assertions from referencing any of its own assertions. A note explains that assertions can be redacted at any point in the asset's provenance history, not only by the claim generator that first used the ingredient; further detail is in section 14.11.3.2 Performing explicit validation.

Specifies that a redacted assertion may either be removed entirely from the assertion store or keep its labelled assertion container with its content boxes replaced by a single UUID Content box carrying the C2PA Redaction UUID (CAA98EEE-9D4D-F80E-86AD-4DFFCA263973) and a DATA field of only zeros. A validator shall accept either representation as validly redacted.
Heading that opens section 14.10.4 Assertion Validation; it carries no text of its own.

Defines the general validation procedure for each hashed_uri in a claim's created_assertions and gathered_assertions (or a v1 claim's assertions). Redacted assertions are treated as valid unless labelled c2pa.actions or c2pa.actions.v2 (rejected with assertion.action.redacted); other assertions must resolve within the same manifest (else assertion.outsideManifest or assertion.missing) and their computed hash must match (else assertion.hashedURI.mismatch, otherwise assertion.hashedURI.match is recorded). The claim shall also be rejected for malformed CBOR or non-conforming JSON (assertion.cbor.invalid or assertion.json.invalid), for assertions in the store that the claim does not reference (assertion.undeclared), and for redacted_assertions URIs pointing into the claim's own manifest (assertion.selfRedacted). Assertion metadata is not validated except that processStart must not be later than processEnd, else assertion.metadata.malformed.

Requires the validator to check each assertion's label and perform the specific validation steps for listed types: c2pa.cloud-data, c2pa.external-reference, c2pa.actions or c2pa.actions.v2, c2pa.linked-resource-integrity, c2pa.metadata, c2pa.session-keys, c2pa.time-stamp and c2pa.alternative-content-representation; unlisted types need no further steps. A note says ingredient assertions are validated separately under section 14.11 Validate the Ingredients. Any hashed_uri or hashed_ext_uri field in a standard assertion shall be validated per section 14.10.4.3 Validation of References, except the activeManifest field of c2pa.ingredient.v3 and the externalResources entries of c2pa.linked-resource-integrity, which have their own procedures.

Specifies validation of c2pa.cloud-data assertions: the label, size and location fields must be present, otherwise rejection with assertion.cloud-data.malformed. The claim shall be rejected with assertion.cloud-data.hardBinding if the external label is a hard binding or multi-asset hash label, with assertion.cloud-data.actions if an update manifest references an actions label, and with assertion.cloud-data.malformed if the label is an actions, cloud-data or ingredient label. The location field is validated per section 14.10.5.2 Validation of External References, and if retrieved, the JUMBF box label must match the label field or the claim is rejected with assertion.cloud-data.labelMismatch.

Specifies validation of c2pa.external-reference assertions: a location field with a url field is required, and location must contain both or neither of alg and hash, otherwise rejection with assertion.external-reference.malformed. When hashed data is retrieved, a hash mismatch is reported as assertion.external-reference.hashMismatch. A label field naming an actions, cloud-data, external-reference, hard binding, multi-asset hash or ingredient label causes rejection with assertion.external-reference.malformed, and a retrieved JUMBF box whose label differs from the label field is reported as assertion.external-reference.labelMismatch.

Specifies validation of c2pa.linked-resource-integrity assertions: the assertion must be in created_assertions (else assertion.linkedResourceIntegrity.notCreated) and its resources field must hold a non-empty externalResources array or a non-empty relativeResources array with an alg field (else assertion.linkedResourceIntegrity.malformed). Each well-formed entry receives exactly one terminal code, including a resourceUrl field: skipped if not retrieved, or match, inaccessible, sizeMismatch, formatMismatch or hashMismatch, none of which cause rejection. External entries need url, alg and hash and follow section 14.10.5.2 Validation of External References with the mismatch codes remapped to informational ones. Relative entries need uri and hash, the shared alg is checked per section 14.4.4 Algorithm validation, and a decoded uri containing a path segment of exactly .. causes rejection with assertion.linkedResourceIntegrity.invalidURI before retrieved data is checked for size, format and hash.

Specifies validation of c2pa.actions and c2pa.actions.v2 assertions, noting that when, whenStart and whenEnd get syntax and consistency checks but shall not be compared to an external time source. An actions field is required, and in v2 when may not appear with whenStart or whenEnd and whenStart must not be later than whenEnd (else assertion.action.malformed); c2pa.created or c2pa.opened is only allowed as the first action of the first actions assertion. Actions c2pa.opened, c2pa.placed, c2pa.removed, c2pa.deleted, c2pa.transcoded and c2pa.repackaged must reference ingredient assertions with the expected relationship and manifest location, otherwise assertion.action.ingredientMismatch (with an informational assertion.action.ingredientLocationMismatch for a v2 claim whose ingredient is listed in a different field). It further covers c2pa.redacted needing a resolvable JUMBF URI (else assertion.action.redactionMismatch), validation of icon fields and relatedAssertions entries, and the requirement that c2pa.watermarked or c2pa.watermarked.bound actions be accompanied by a c2pa.soft-binding assertion (else assertion.action.softBindingMissing).

States that c2pa.metadata needs no assertion-specific validation. Although generators are still required to limit metadata to the allowed list, validators should not reject assertions containing unlisted fields, to support forward compatibility, unlike earlier versions of the specification.

Requires a validator to ensure that the signerBinding signature of a c2pa.session-keys assertion is correct, by verifying it validates using the session key and that its payload is the Signer's end-entity certificate. Session keys are valid only if this signature validates successfully.

Requires a validator to ensure that a c2pa.time-stamp assertion is well-formed CBOR consisting of a single map with at least one key/value pair, otherwise rejecting the claim with assertion.timestamp.malformed. Because the time stamp token is validated as described in section 14.8.2 Validating the TimeStampToken, the validator needs to store it and its associated C2PA Manifest identifier for later use.

Specifies validation of c2pa.alternative-content-representation assertions whose type is exif.originalPreservationImage: at most one such assertion may appear in the active manifest, and exactly one of multiAssetPartIndex or embeddedOriginalPreservationImage must be present, else rejection with assertion.alternativeContentRepresentation.malformed. A multiAssetPartIndex requires a c2pa.hash.multi-asset assertion and must be an in-bounds index into its parts array. An embeddedOriginalPreservationImage must be a hashed-uri-map with a hash field whose value matches the computed hash of the resolved data, else assertion.alternativeContentRepresentation.hashMismatch; if no failures occur, assertion.alternativeContentRepresentation.match is recorded.

Describes how hashed_uri and hashed_ext_uri references in standard assertions are validated, excluding the activeManifest field of c2pa.ingredient.v3 and the externalResources entries of c2pa.linked-resource-integrity. A retrieved hashed_ext_uri follows section 14.10.5.2 Validation of External References. For a hashed_uri, a missing url or unlocatable destination is a validation failure with hashedURI.missing; otherwise the algorithm is determined per section 14.4, and a missing hash field or a mismatch with the computed hash causes rejection with hashedURI.mismatch.
Heading that opens section 14.10.5 External Data Validation; it carries no text of its own.

States that externally hosted data referenced by cloud data or hashed external reference assertions is not retrieved during standard validation; a validator shall first successfully validate the claim and shall not retrieve external data from a rejected claim. Because retrieval is optional, failure to retrieve or validate external data shall not cause rejection. A validator that does retrieve such data shall follow section 14.10.5.2 Validation of External References, may apply the countermeasures of section 14.10.5.3 Retrieval Security, and shall validate retrieved labelled assertions as if they were embedded.

Specifies the procedure for validating external data from cloud data or hashed external reference assertions. The validator resolves the url and aborts if it is missing, a countermeasure is applied, or retrieval fails; it then returns assertion.hashedURI.mismatch without providing the data if the retrieved representation's length differs from size or its Content-Type differs from the declared content type (from dc:format, defaulting to application/jumbf for cloud data, with content_type ignored). For a hashed_ext_uri, the hash is computed with the algorithm determined per section 14.4.3 For Hashed Ext URIs; a missing or mismatched hash yields assertion.hashedURI.mismatch, otherwise assertion.hashedURI.match is recorded and the data is provided to the application.

Permits a validator performing network retrieval to apply the countermeasures in this section before and during each retrieval attempt, regardless of which assertion type triggered it. If retrieval is done by a platform the validator does not control and cannot apply the countermeasures, the validator may route retrieval through a component that can, such as a server-side service, or may decline to retrieve. A note gives a browser-based validator as an example and recalls that skipping optional retrieval does not cause a claim to be rejected.

Permits a validator to limit automated retrieval to the https URI scheme and to decline other schemes such as file or ftp and non-network identifiers, noting that unencrypted http is discouraged by industry practice. A validator may also reject a URI whose authority contains a userinfo subcomponent before attempting retrieval.

Permits a validator to omit ambient credentials such as cookies, Authorization headers, proxy credentials or client certificates from retrieval requests unless the operator has explicitly configured them for that specific origin. A validator may also withhold credentials attached for one origin from a different origin reached through a redirect.

Permits a validator to resolve the target host before connecting and check each candidate IP address against an address policy, disallowing loopback, link-local, private-use, unique-local or other non-publicly-routable addresses unless the operator explicitly permits them, and aborting if all candidates are disallowed. The validator may also bind the connection to a checked address, verify the actual peer address before sending data, and treat any later name resolution, including by a library or proxy, as subject to the same policy. Where the operator configures a resolving proxy, these checks may be delegated to it, and the proxy's own address is not subject to the policy. Notes explain that operator configuration supports enterprise private networks and synthetic-address tunnelling services, that the restriction exists because the URI comes from the manifest author, and that retrieval can disclose the requested hostname, which encrypted DNS, a remote-resolving proxy, or not retrieving can reduce.

Permits a validator to limit the number of HTTP redirects it follows per validation operation and to refuse HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects, aborting retrieval if either occurs. Before sending a redirected request, a validator may apply the scheme, credential and address countermeasures of sections 14.10.5.3.1 to 14.10.5.3.3 to the redirect target exactly as for the initial request.

Defines the retrieved representation used for the size, media type and hash checks in section 14.10.5.2 Validation of External References as the response body bytes after removing HTTP transfer coding and any Content-Encoding, but before any character decoding, parsing, normalization or other transformation. Requires all three checks to be performed against this same representation.

Defines a retrieval attempt as a single request-response exchange and a validation operation as the full process of resolving, retrieving, decoding and validating the data for one hashed_ext_uri, unhashed_ext_uri or cloud data location, including redirects. Permits a validator to enforce per-operation limits on redirects, encoded bytes read, decoded representation bytes, decompression nesting depth and an overall deadline, and per-claim limits on total retrieval attempts and concurrent operations. If an enforced limit is exceeded, the validator may abort and discard partial data; a note says the size field gives an a priori bound on decoded bytes usable as a read limit.
Heading that opens section 14.11 Validate the Ingredients; it carries no text of its own.

Requires a validator to perform the validation steps for the presented asset and its active manifest, rejecting the manifest with the indicated failure code if any step finds it invalid. Explains that an active manifest may list ingredients via ingredient assertions, some of which may have their own manifests with further ingredients.
Heading that opens section 14.11.2 Processing Ingredient Manifests; it carries no text of its own.
Requires that, when processing a standard manifest, a validator validate each ingredient regardless of its relationship value, as described in section 14.11.3 Ingredient Assertion Validation.
Requires that, for update manifests, the parentOf ingredient be validated as described in section 14.11.3 Ingredient Assertion Validation.

Requires that any time stamp manifests found in an ingredient be ignored, noting that this feature is deprecated in favour of the time stamp assertion and the text is retained for historical purposes.
Heading that opens section 14.11.3 Ingredient Assertion Validation; it carries no text of its own.

Presents Figure 13, Ingredient Validation, a flowchart of the process for validating ingredient assertions in a C2PA Manifest, and notes that the text is authoritative where it differs from the figure.

Specifies explicit checks on ingredient assertions, each failing with assertion.ingredient.malformed: the relationship field must be present and be parentOf, inputTo or componentOf, and activeManifest and digitalSourceType must not both be present. If relatedAssertions is present it must be a non-empty array whose hashed URIs validate per section 14.10.4.3 and resolve to assertions in the same manifest that are not ingredient or actions assertions and whose label ends with .ingredient, ignoring any multiple-instance suffix. A referenced assertion that has been redacted causes the informational code assertion.redacted to be recorded.

Requires the validator to recursively validate all ingredient manifests, with results equivalent to the described depth-first algorithm. The algorithm collects lists of ingredient manifest hashed_uri tuples (activeManifest or c2pa_manifest plus claimSignature) and redacted assertion JUMBF URIs across the lineage, rejecting with claim.missing or assertion.selfRedacted where appropriate, skipping unresolvable, mismatched or zeroed ingredient assertions and returning any validationResults status codes. Each ingredient manifest with matching redacted assertions is then validated by the claim signature hash method, otherwise by either that method or the manifest hash method, with validationResults entries reconciled against the validation output. A v3 ingredient with activeManifest but no validationResults yields assertion.ingredient.malformed, and validators should ignore other manifests in the store that are not in the ingredient list, for compatibility with custom and future constructs.

Describes the claim signature hash validation method, a full validation of the ingredient's claim without evaluating content bindings. The claimSignature url is resolved (else ingredient.claimSignature.missing) and its hash compared with the hash field, rejecting with ingredient.claimSignature.mismatch if absent or unequal; on a match, ingredient.claimSignature.validated is issued and the signature, time stamp and revocation information are validated per sections 14.7 to 14.9. Redacted assertions with a matching manifest label that contain anything other than zero bytes cause rejection with assertion.notRedacted, and non-redacted assertions other than hard bindings are validated per section 14.10. Under this method the validator shall not record hash mismatch codes for activeManifest, and notes explain that only c2pa.ingredient.v3 has a claimSignature field, so redactions in manifests referenced by deprecated ingredient assertions cause validation to fail.

Describes the manifest hash validation method, a faster option for an ingredient manifest unchanged by redaction when the validator trusts the previous claim generator's results. The activeManifest url is resolved (else ingredient.manifest.missing), its hash computed per section 14.4 and section 9.4.2.3, and compared with the hash field; a missing or unequal hash causes rejection with ingredient.manifest.mismatch, while a match fully validates the ingredient and issues ingredient.manifest.validated.

Requires the asset's content to be validated using the hard binding in the active manifest if it is a standard manifest, or, for an update manifest, by following the chain of parentOf ingredients to the first standard manifest. If no standard manifest is found or it has no hard binding in created_assertions, the active manifest's claim shall be rejected with claim.hardBindings.missing. Notes that an asset may consist of multiple parts with their own hashes, per section 16.3.5 Multi-Asset Hash, which may be validated separately.
Heading that opens section 14.12.1 Validating a data hash; it carries no text of its own.

Specifies validation of a c2pa.hash.data assertion: overlapping or negative exclusion ranges cause rejection with assertion.dataHash.malformed, and when update manifests are present the C2PA Manifest Store exclusion length and later range starts are adjusted for the store's current length. The hash is computed over the asset bytes outside the exclusion ranges; an exclusion running past the end of the asset, a missing hash field, or non-permitted data within the manifest store exclusion causes rejection with assertion.dataHash.mismatch, and an unlisted alg causes algorithm.unsupported. Additional exclusions beyond the manifest store and padding produce the informational code assertion.dataHash.additionalExclusionsPresent, pad and pad2 fields are ignored, and success yields assertion.dataHash.match. If the hash does not match, a multi-asset hash assertion is validated if present, otherwise the manifest is rejected with assertion.dataHash.mismatch.

Specifies that in JPEG 1 files the file format extras include APP11 markers and their segment length bytes, and requires a validator to match the total exclusion range length against the total length of all APP11 segments holding the C2PA Manifest to detect tampering. A note says APP11 segments used for other purposes, such as JPEG 360 or JPEG Privacy and Security, are not included.
Heading that opens section 14.12.1.3 Hashing of Unstructured Text; it carries no text of its own.

Specifies how validators shall validate a c2pa.hash.data hard binding for unstructured text with an embedded C2PATextManifestWrapper. The validator locates all valid wrappers (accepting decoded streams of at least manifestLength + 13 bytes and ignoring trailing padding), identifies the wrapper whose byte range, including padding, matches the exclusions, and rejects with assertion.dataHash.malformed if none matches. It then removes the wrapper bytes, normalizes the remaining text to NFC, encodes it as UTF-8, hashes it with the alg of the assertion, and records assertion.dataHash.match on a match or rejects with assertion.dataHash.mismatch otherwise.

Lists the standard result codes for text validation: assertion.dataHash.match for success, assertion.dataHash.mismatch for a hash mismatch indicating tampering, and assertion.dataHash.malformed for a malformed data hash assertion such as invalid exclusion ranges.

Explains that partially copied unstructured text may have a truncated or absent C2PATextManifestWrapper that cannot be decoded, so the asset is treated as if no manifests were located. A validator may indicate to the user that the content appears to be a fragment of a larger asset.

Requires that for structured text assets the data hash be computed over the raw file bytes with the manifest block excluded via the exclusion range, following the general data hash procedure of section 12.2.2 Hard Bindings. A note explains that no Unicode normalization is applied because structured text files are byte-stable and NFC could cause false mismatches for legitimate NFD content, and that ASCII delimiters make the manifest block boundaries unambiguous.

Requires that for ONNX files the data hash be computed over the raw bytes of the serialized ModelProto with the Base64-encoded c2pa:manifest value excluded, following section 12.2.2 Hard Bindings. A validator shall verify that exactly one StringStringEntryProto with key c2pa:manifest exists in ModelProto.metadata_props, treating the asset as having no manifests if there is more than one, and shall verify that the exclusion range matches the offset and length of the Base64-encoded manifest value.

Requires that for SafeTensors files the data hash be computed over the complete file (8-byte header length, JSON header and tensor data) with the Base64-encoded c2pa:manifest value excluded, following section 12.2.2 Hard Bindings. A validator shall verify that exactly one c2pa:manifest key exists in the __metadata__ object, treating the asset as having no manifests if there is more than one, and shall reject the asset with assertion.dataHash.malformed if the header length field does not match the actual JSON header length.

Specifies validation of BMFF hashes: rendered content shall be validated against its hard binding per section 12.2.2, falling back to a multi-asset hash if present, and any failure or missing bound content shall be clearly signalled to the user and continue to be reported. For streamed or progressively downloaded content, not-yet-available portions are not failures, but each portion shall be validated before rendering and its sequence checked, with unexpected discontinuities signalled and Merkle location values required to start at zero and increment by one; content not rendered as intended, such as fast-forward, may be signalled as unvalidatable. With an update ContentProvenanceBox, the active manifest is searched there first and the parentOf chain followed to the first non-update manifest, whose BMFF hash is validated. The manifest is rejected with assertion.bmffHash.malformed for missing or empty exclusions, fragmented assets with both hash and merkle, or overlapping or negative subset ranges; extra exclusions yield assertion.bmffHash.additionalExclusionsPresent, pad fields are ignored, success yields assertion.bmffHash.match, and a mismatch defers to a multi-asset hash assertion if present.

Specifies Merkle tree validation for non-fragmented BMFF assets: without fixedBlockSize or variableBlockSizes the whole mdat payload is one leaf, with fixedBlockSize it is split into fixed blocks (the last block should be truncated to the payload end), and with variableBlockSizes it is split per that array, which must match count and the payload size. Having both block size fields, or a count smaller than the computed leaf nodes, causes rejection with assertion.bmffHash.malformed. Leaf hashes that do not match merkle-map.hashes cause rejection with assertion.bmffHash.mismatch, and when count exceeds the number of hashes the auxiliary uuid C2PA box is required, else assertion.bmffHash.malformed.

Requires that for fragmented BMFF assets with a merkle field the validator validate the Merkle tree, rejecting the manifest with assertion.bmffHash.malformed if the auxiliary uuid C2PA box is missing and with assertion.bmffHash.mismatch if the hash computed from that box and leaf node does not match the corresponding entry in merkle-map.hashes.

Specifies validation of a c2pa.hash.boxes assertion: the boxes field must be present (else assertion.boxesHash.malformed), boxes must appear in the asset in the listed order (else assertion.boxesHash.mismatch), and unlisted boxes cause assertion.boxesHash.unknownBox. The hash algorithm is taken from the box-hash-map, box-map or Claim alg in that order, with algorithm.unsupported if none is valid; exclusion ranges are relative to the box given by boxIndex and must exist, not overlap and not be negative (else assertion.boxesHash.malformed), and missing names fields are also malformed. Hashes are computed over each box or range of named boxes, skipping exclusions and boxes marked excluded; data in the manifest store exclusion other than the store and padding, exclusions running past a box, or a missing or mismatched hash cause assertion.boxesHash.mismatch, with fallback to a multi-asset hash if present. Extra exclusions yield assertion.boxesHash.additionalExclusionsPresent, pad fields are ignored, and success yields assertion.boxesHash.match.

Requires a validator of a JPEG 1 asset to check that each box marked with the C2PA identifier is an APP11 containing part or all of the C2PA Manifest Store, identified as a JUMBF superbox labelled c2pa with type UUID 63327061-0011-0010-8000-00AA00389B71. An APP11 not part of the store and not in the hashed boxes list causes rejection with assertion.boxesHash.unknownBox.

States that in JPEG-XL the C2PA Manifest Store is a top-level JUMBF box, and requires the box containing it to be identified with the special C2PA box identifier; the store is recognised as a JUMBF superbox labelled c2pa with type UUID 63327061-0011-0010-8000-00AA00389B71.

Requires a validator of a font to check that the box for the font's C2PA table is present and determine whether it holds an embedded manifest, a remote manifest URI or both. Font tables not covered by any box cause rejection with assertion.boxesHash.unknownBox.

Specifies that if standard hard binding validation fails and a multi-asset hash assertion is in created_assertions, the validator shall validate it; more than one such assertion, a missing or empty parts array, or a part lacking a valid locator and hashAssertion causes rejection with assertion.multiAssetHash.malformed. Byte-offset locators need non-negative byteOffset and length, and bmffBox locators must reference a present box. A missing non-optional part causes assertion.multiAssetHash.missingPart while optional parts are skipped, and overlapping parts or parts not covering every byte cause assertion.multiAssetHash.malformed. Each part is hashed with its referenced method using offsets relative to the part start, with truncation or mismatch causing assertion.multiAssetHash.mismatch; if all parts validate, assertion.multiAssetHash.match is recorded and no hard binding failure codes are recorded.
Heading that opens section 14.12.5 Validating a collection data hash; it carries no text of its own.

Specifies validation of a c2pa.hash.collection.data assertion by iterating over its uris array, rejecting with assertion.collectionHash.malformed if uris is missing or any entry lacks uri or hash. Each uri shall be checked before use and rejected with assertion.collectionHash.invalidURI if it contains . or ..; each retrieved asset is hashed over all its bytes, with a mismatch causing assertion.collectionHash.mismatch and a match adding assertion.collectionHash.match. Any listed file not found causes rejection with assertion.collectionHash.incorrectFileCount.

States that for ZIP files the collection data hash includes a zip_central_directory_hash field hashing every central directory header and the end of central directory record with the same algorithm as the hash field. A validator shall check that this field is present and matches, rejecting the manifest with assertion.collectionHash.mismatch otherwise.

Specifies that for WARC files the collection data hash covers every record except the C2PA manifest record, each hashed over its uncompressed bytes. Because WARC has no central directory, a validator shall reject with assertion.collectionHash.mismatch if any two non-manifest records share a WARC-Record-ID, and shall verify that records and uris entries correspond one-to-one by matching uri to WARC-Record-ID, rejecting with the same code otherwise, so that appended or duplicated records cannot leave the manifest valid. Compressed records shall be decompressed under an implementation-defined maximum size and rejected with assertion.collectionHash.mismatch if they exceed it or if the decompressed length differs from Content-Length, which a note explains bounds work from maliciously crafted records.
Heading that opens section 14.12.6 Validating a segment hash; it carries no text of its own.

Specifies validation of a c2pa.hash.segment assertion over the file read in binary mode. The manifest is rejected with assertion.segmentHash.malformed if version is missing or unrecognised, if hash, segmentStart or segmentEnd is missing or segmentEnd is less than segmentStart, if predecessorSentinel lacks start, length or hash, or if sentinelLength presence does not match whether the sentinel line references the store externally (required) or inline (forbidden). The sentinel line must begin at segmentEnd, and the hash over bytes [segmentStart, segmentEnd) must match, otherwise assertion.segmentHash.mismatch; on success assertion.segmentHash.match is added.

Requires that the checkpoints in a file together cover every byte. For the active checkpoint, the end boundary (segmentEnd plus sentinelLength, or plus the actual sentinel line length including its line ending) must equal the file length, the first checkpoint without predecessorSentinel must have segmentStart of 0, and every other checkpoint's segmentStart must equal predecessorSentinel.start plus predecessorSentinel.length; any failure causes rejection with assertion.segmentHash.partialCoverage. A note says these checks ensure every byte up to the active sentinel line falls in exactly one segment or sentinel line, with no gaps.

Describes validating the chain of checkpoints, where each later checkpoint records its predecessor's sentinel line position and digest and references its manifest as a parentOf ingredient. Starting from the active checkpoint, for each checkpoint with predecessorSentinel the validator shall hash the referenced bytes (rejecting with assertion.segmentHash.predecessorMismatch on mismatch), obtain the preceding manifest store from them, and validate its segment hash assertion per sections 14.12.6.1 and 14.12.6.2; a checkpoint without predecessorSentinel completes the chain. If an earlier checkpoint's externally stored manifest cannot be retrieved, the validator shall report manifest.inaccessible and treat that and all earlier segments as unverified, but shall not reject the active checkpoint on that basis alone.
Heading that opens section 15 Live Media; it carries no text of its own.

Introduces the C2PA Live Media specification as supporting live, streaming and dynamic packaging workflows where content is created or packaged in real time, and outlining how to manage assertions for tracks in live sessions to ensure integrity and authenticity. Notes clarify that it covers live streaming and dynamic packaging and is not limited to video, provided the packaging is BMFF or delivery uses Enhanced RTMP (V2). States that this version applies to ISO BMFF content, ISO/IEC 23000-19 content, and Enhanced RTMP (V2) contributions via section 15.5 Verifiable Segment Info method, while being agnostic of manifest and delivery protocols, and does not support MPEG-2 Transport Streams.

States that beginning with version 2.5 the term live video was renamed live media to reflect broader scope, with live video now considered a subset. Identifiers originally defined with livevideo nomenclature, including CDDL rule and file names, assertion labels and validation failure codes, are retained without renaming for compatibility.
Heading that opens section 15.3 Architecture; it carries no text of its own.

Describes live media manifest transport as building on BMFF embedding with two key requirements: content hashing shall use a standard bmff-hash-map targeting a segment (or the method of section 15.5.3 for Enhanced RTMP (V2)), and any C2PA Manifest Store in a live stream shall be in a uuid box per section A.5.1, or for Enhanced RTMP (V2) in a c2paManifest pair in a VideoPacketType.Metadata or AudioPacketType.Metadata message. The uuid box holding a manifest store may appear in any segment and is called the C2PA Manifest Box. Defines dynamically packaged content as prepared just-in-time on request, treats live media and dynamically packaged content as interchangeable terms, and notes that live streams are always dynamically packaged but not vice versa.

States that live or dynamically packaged streams require each segment to be validated independently, so each segment must carry its own content hash. Describes two signing methods, either of which can be used and validators need not support both: section 15.4 Per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method and section 15.5 Verifiable Segment Info method, the latter using a verifiable-segment-info in an emsg box or E-RTMP Metadata message together with session keys. Other C2PA-defined live media binding schemes may be used provided they compute segment hashes with a standard bmff-hash-map and embed or reference the manifest store via a uuid box per section A.5.1.

Requires that, where an initialization segment is used, it contain a uuid box whose bmff-hash-map includes the moov box, cryptographically linking it to the media segments. In broadcast push scenarios the initialization segment may be repeated periodically and the uuid box need not be in every copy. A note explains the binding ensures the manifest corresponds to the specific media, preventing replay attacks and content substitution.
Heading that opens section 15.4 Per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method; it carries no text of its own.

Describes the per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method, which a live media stream may use: each media segment shall contain a C2PA Manifest Box in a uuid box per section A.5.1, whose active manifest shall contain a c2pa.hash.bmff.v3 assertion with a hash covering the segment and no merkle field, plus a live media segment assertion, and may contain other relevant assertions. Claim generators may embed additional per-segment validation values derived from segment hashes, such as anchor-point chaining values. A note says this method does not need session keys, verifiable-segment-info-map or emsg boxes and can be used independently of the Verifiable Segment Info method.

Requires a live media segment assertion labelled c2pa.livevideo.segment in each segment's manifest when using the per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method, containing a sequenceNumber identifying the segment and a streamId identifying the whole stream (any unique string, such as a UUID or URL). It shall also contain a continuityMethod field indicating how cryptographic continuity between segments is ensured; the only defined value is c2pa.manifestId, which requires a previousManifestId field holding the previous segment's manifest identifier. Implementers may define other continuity methods and fields, named using labels as described in section 8.2 Labels.

Gives the CDDL schema for the live media segment assertion via the livevideo-segment-map rule, with sequenceNumber, streamId, continuityMethod and optional additional fields, and the livevideo-segment-map-manifestId rule adding previousManifestId when continuityMethod is c2pa.manifestId; the complete normative schema is in section G.8.1 Live Media Segment. Also provides a CBOR diagnostic notation example of such an assertion.
Heading that opens section 15.5 Verifiable Segment Info method; it carries no text of its own.

Defines the verifiable-segment-info as a COSE_Sign1_Tagged structure giving concise per-segment information so each live media segment can be validated independently, used in workflows that sign segment information with session keys. Its payload is a CBOR-serialized segment-info-map that shall be present and not detached, signed by a private session key, with alg (and optionally iat) in the protected header and the session key kid in the unprotected header. The segment-info-map shall contain sequenceNumber (matching mfhd.sequence_number or the ISO/IEC 23009-9 indexing rules, and matching the live media segment assertion when both methods are used), manifestId identifying the current or still-active manifest, and bmffHash, a bmff-hash-map of the segment with no merkle field and an exclusion for /emsg boxes with value urn:c2pa:verifiable-segment-info. It may also contain an optional manifestUri hashed-ext-uri from which a manifest can be retrieved.

Requires that, in workflows using the verifiable-segment-info method, a verifiable-segment-info be present in the emsg box of each segment, noting this does not apply to workflows relying only on per-segment C2PA Manifest Boxes. Specifies the emsg field values: version 0, scheme_id_uri urn:c2pa:verifiable-segment-info, value fseg, presentation_time_delta 0, timescale and event_duration covering the segment, a session-unique id, and message_data holding the encoded verifiable-segment-info. Gives the CDDL schema for verifiable-segment-info and segment-info-map, with the complete normative schema in section G.8.2 Verifiable Segment Info.

Describes carriage over Enhanced RTMP (V2), a message-based streaming protocol used for live contribution that does not use ISO BMFF packaging. For such content, rtmp-verifiable-segment-info is carried in a VideoPacketType.Metadata or AudioPacketType.Metadata message instead of an emsg box, with an rtmp-segment-info-map payload whose sequenceNumber and manifestId have the same meaning as before and whose segmentHash, an rtmp-hash-map, replaces bmffHash. A note says AudioPacketType.Metadata is not yet defined by Enhanced RTMP (V2) and its use assumes it will be added.

Defines a logical segment for Enhanced RTMP (V2) content: tracks are identified by media type and trackId (non-multitrack messages belong to track 0, and an absent trackId equals 0), and a segment is scoped to one track, with the carrying Metadata message required to belong to that track. A video or audio segment shall begin at the tag header of the first frame after the previous segment and consist of complete frames followed by one or more Metadata messages carrying rtmp-verifiable-segment-info. Publishers shall send Metadata messages on the same chunk stream as the track's coded frames, with a timestamp equal to the segment's last frame, which a note says guarantees unambiguous ordering. Consecutive Metadata messages belong to the segment they close, boundaries shall not split frames, sequenceNumber shall increase by 1 per segment per track, and each session key shall sign for only one track.

Specifies that segmentHash in an rtmp-segment-info-map shall be computed with the alg algorithm over the concatenation, in transmission order, of each coded-frame packet's RTMP message timestamp (32-bit unsigned big-endian), composition time offset (24-bit signed big-endian, or 0 if absent) and coded media data. Only the segment's track packet from a Multitrack message is included, Aggregate Message contents are treated as individually transmitted with normalized timestamps, and no other bytes are included. Notes clarify that control messages, data messages, codec configuration packets and all Metadata messages do not contribute, that rewriting timestamps or composition offsets invalidates the hash, and that the TimestampOffsetNano ModEx data is not covered and so cannot be relied upon by a validator.

Requires a manifest delivered in a c2paManifest pair to use as its hard binding a data hash assertion without exclusions, computed over the E-RTMP initialization data, defined as the concatenated codec configuration payloads from each track's most recent SequenceStart packet (or legacy sequence header), video tracks before audio and by ascending trackId. Publishers shall send each track's codec configuration on that track's chunk stream and before the binding c2paManifest, sending a new c2paManifest before dependent frames if configuration changes. A validator shall validate this hard binding when it validates the first segment whose manifestId identifies that manifest, against the configuration most recently received before that segment's closing c2paSegmentInfo. Notes explain this mirrors binding to the moov box, that onMetaData is excluded because intermediaries rewrite it, and that multiple message streams on one connection share one manifest and so must not reuse a media type and trackId combination.

Requires AMF3 object encoding in VideoPacketType.Metadata and AudioPacketType.Metadata messages, with the c2paSegmentInfo and c2paManifest values carried as native AMF3 ByteArray. c2paSegmentInfo holds the binary rtmp-verifiable-segment-info in the Metadata messages closing each segment; several may appear for one segment, for example during key rotation, and the segment is valid if at least one validates. c2paManifest holds a binary C2PA Manifest Store that shall include a c2pa.session-keys assertion, sent for the first manifest and whenever the active manifest changes, and should be on the video track unless an audio track needs its own manifest. Gives the CDDL schema for rtmp-segment-info-map (normative schema in section G.8.3 Enhanced RTMP Segment Info) and a CBOR diagnostic example.

Requires C2PA Manifest support over E-RTMP to be negotiated in the connection handshake using the C2PA bit (0x10) of CapsExMask: a supporting client shall set it in the capsEx property of its connect Command Object and set objectEncoding to 3, and a supporting server shall set it in the Info Object of its _result. An endpoint shall not send c2paSegmentInfo or c2paManifest unless both sides signaled support, and a non-signaling endpoint should not expect them. Receivers shall ignore unrecognized pairs in Metadata messages and continue processing the rest; a note says negotiation avoids depending on legacy endpoint behaviour.

States that an Enhanced RTMP (V2) reconnection does not affect a stream's C2PA state (active manifest, session keys and per-track sequenceNumber), so segments on the new connection shall continue each track's sequenceNumber. After reconnecting, a publisher shall resend the active manifest in a c2paManifest pair after each track's codec configuration and before the first coded frame. Notes explain that this supports moving to a different server instance, and that segments cannot span a reconnection, so a publisher can send each track's current c2paSegmentInfo before disconnecting to avoid unvalidatable frames.

Requires that when a new segment needs different assertions, such as changed provenance or replacement of expiring session keys, a new C2PA Manifest Store be provided, embedded in a C2PA Manifest Box, linked externally, or for E-RTMP via a c2paManifest pair in a Metadata message. The new manifest shall apply to all subsequent segments until another is provided, which a note says allows dynamic updates while maintaining integrity and authenticity.
Heading that opens section 15.5.5 Session Keys; it carries no text of its own.

Describes session keys as asymmetric key pairs that may use any algorithm allowed for claim generator X.509 certificates; they shall be generated at the start of a live media session, may also be delivered in later manifests, are each used for a limited period to enable rotation, and should be updated when provenance changes. Public keys are delivered in a C2PA Manifest, with the initial set in the initialization segment's manifest or, for E-RTMP, in a c2paManifest sent before the referencing c2paSegmentInfo. For an unknown session key, a receiver should check the segment's C2PA Manifest Box, then the manifestUri, and shall fall back to the initialization segment's manifest; for E-RTMP it shall use the c2paManifest matching manifestId and should try manifestUri if needed. The receiver shall ensure the retrieved manifest's identifier matches manifestId, and an externally hosted manifest needs to remain at its URI for as long as the content is provided.
Describes the session keys assertion as the means of carrying one or more public session keys inside a C2PA Manifest, and points to the Session Keys Assertion section for its full description.
Introduces Figure 14, Live Media Architecture, which shows the general scheme of the data structures that can be used in a live media workflow and how each connects to the others.
Heading that opens section 15.7 Live Media Generation Process; it carries no text of its own.

Specifies that, with the per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method, each segment's C2PA Manifest is constructed as described in Section A.5, Embedding manifests into BMFF-based assets, except that the bmff-hash-map hashes only that segment's bytes. Requires that a Live Media Segment Assertion (Section 15.4.2) be included in the manifest to provide metadata about the segment.

Describes the two steps of generating a live media stream with the Verifiable Segment Info method. In session key generation, one or more session keys, each with its own createdAt, validityPeriod and minSequenceNumber, are included in the C2PA Manifest in the C2PA Manifest Box that shall be present in the initialization segment(s), or in an E-RTMP VideoPacketType.Metadata or AudioPacketType.Metadata message; minSequenceNumber indicates the earliest segment that should be signed with that key, supporting overlap for key rotation. In signing the box hash, each BMFF/CMAF segment shall have an emsg box containing the verifiable-segment-info, a segment-info-map signed by a session key that carries a sequenceNumber against out-of-order attacks and a bmff-hash-map hashing the segment, and an updated manifest may be included in the segment or referenced via manifestUri. Notes explain that over Enhanced RTMP (V2) each track uses its own session key and an rtmp-verifiable-segment-info with an rtmp-segment-info-map is carried in Metadata messages, and that longer streams rotate session keys through subsequent initialization segments.
Heading that opens section 15.8 Live Media Validation Process; it carries no text of its own.

Specifies the initial validation steps common to live media segments. An initialization segment containing an mdat box fails with livevideo.init.invalid; a BMFF/CMAF segment with neither a C2PA Manifest Box nor a conforming emsg box, or an E-RTMP segment not closed by Metadata messages carrying a conforming c2paSegmentInfo, fails with livevideo.segment.invalid. A C2PA Manifest Box found in a segment shall be validated per Chapter 14, Validation, failing with livevideo.manifest.invalid if it does not validate. For Enhanced RTMP (V2) content, the validator shall have obtained the C2PA Manifest identified by the manifestId of the rtmp-segment-info-map (else livevideo.init.invalid), shall validate it with its hard binding checked against the E-RTMP initialization data, and shall fail the segment with livevideo.init.invalid if any coded frame's most recent codec configuration is not the one bound by that manifest.

Lists the tests a validator shall perform when the C2PA Manifest in a segment's C2PA Manifest Box contains a live media segment assertion. The sequenceNumber must exceed that of the previous segment (unless it is the first) and the streamId must match the previous segment's, otherwise livevideo.assertion.invalid; continuityMethod must be present, otherwise livevideo.continuityMethod.invalid. If continuityMethod is "c2pa.manifestId", a previousManifestId field is required (else livevideo.continuityMethod.invalid) and must match the previous segment's manifestId (else livevideo.segment.invalid), and any other continuity method the validator does not recognize or support fails with livevideo.continuityMethod.invalid.

Specifies how a validator processes the Verifiable Segment Info method: public session keys from a session keys assertion are extracted and stored, and a key that does not conform or whose signerBinding signature fails is invalid and causes livevideo.sessionkey.invalid. A non-initialization segment with a conforming emsg box but no valid session keys fails with livevideo.segment.invalid; otherwise the validator uses the kid from the unprotected header to find the key, retrieving the manifest via manifestUri if needed, and fails with livevideo.segment.invalid if the key is missing or the signature does not verify. The segment-info-map check also fails with livevideo.segment.invalid if the sequenceNumber does not increase, is below the key's minSequenceNumber, the BMFF/CMAF presentation time is outside the key's validity period, or the hash does not match bmffHash. The validator should also check that the certificate that signed the manifest providing the current session key is still valid, failing with livevideo.sessionkey.invalid if it is not.

Specifies that for content contributed over Enhanced RTMP (V2) the Verifiable Segment Info validation steps apply, with the Metadata message carrying c2paSegmentInfo used in place of the emsg box and the rtmp-segment-info-map segmentHash field used in place of bmffHash, and session keys delivered in c2pa.session-keys in a c2paManifest metadata message. Lists the errors that cause livevideo.segment.invalid when parsing the rtmp-segment-info-map: a non-increasing sequenceNumber within a track, a sequenceNumber below the key's minSequenceNumber, validation time outside the key's createdAt plus validityPeriod window, a hash mismatch with segmentHash, a key identified by kid already used for a different track, or a Metadata message that does not belong to the track identified by its mediaType and trackId.
Heading that opens section 16 C2PA Standard Assertions; it carries no text of its own.

Introduces the standard set of assertions for C2PA implementations, noting that example JUMBF URIs are shortened for illustration. Requires all assertions to have a label per Section 8.2, Labels, and to be versioned per Chapter 5, Versioning; standardized assertions use the JSON, CBOR or Embedded File JUMBF content types from ISO 19566-5:2023, entity-specific assertions may use others, and the Codestream content type shall not be used. Unless otherwise stated, standard assertions shall be serialized as CBOR complying with the Core Deterministic Encoding Requirements of RFC 8949 with CDDL schemas, while JSON assertions use JSON Schema. Explains that the assertions are grouped into functional clusters, and that Metadata About Assertions and Regions of Interest are supporting structures used by assertions rather than assertions themselves.

Lists the standard C2PA assertions in Table 3, grouped by function (content binding and integrity, provenance and workflow, ingredient, content description and referencing, trust and validation adjuncts, policy and disclosure), giving each type's assertion labels, schema and serialization. Examples include c2pa.hash.data, c2pa.hash.bmff.v3 (with c2pa.hash.bmff removed and c2pa.hash.bmff.v2 deprecated), c2pa.actions.v2, c2pa.ingredient.v3, c2pa.metadata (JSON-LD), c2pa.session-keys and c2pa.ai-disclosure.

Describes the content binding and integrity assertions as those that bind a manifest to an asset's content and let a Manifest Consumer detect tampering, using either cryptographic hashes of the asset's bytes or soft (perceptual) bindings.
Heading that opens section 16.3.1 Data Hash; it carries no text of its own.

Describes the data hash assertion as the most common hard binding for non-BMFF-based assets, recommending the general box hash assertion for box-like formats not compatible with BMFF. The optional alg field shall name an allowed algorithm (otherwise the Claim's alg applies), the hash goes in the hash field, and excluded ranges shall be listed in exclusions in increasing start order without overlap. Exclusion ranges shall begin and end within one logical unit without overlapping its header or length fields (except freebox or pad data), and the claim generator shall ensure they contain only C2PA Manifest Store content or asset metadata and cannot materially affect interpretation of the asset. The deprecated url field shall not be added and shall be ignored by consumers, and the assertion shall be labelled c2pa.hash.data and shall not appear in a cloud data or external reference assertion nor be used with a compressed manifest.

Specifies the CDDL schema for the data hash assertion (the data-hash-map rule, with optional exclusions, alg, pad2, name and deprecated url, and required hash and pad), with the full normative schema in Section G.4.1, and gives a CBOR diagnostic example. Requires exclusion start and length values to use preferred (shortest) serialization normally, but to be written as 32-bit integers when they are not yet known. Requires pad to be present as a zero-filled byte string and pad2, if present, to be zero-filled, with Section 11.7, Multiple Step Processing, describing how to fill in values and adjust padding.

Requires that, when hashing a JPEG 1 file into which the C2PA Manifest will be embedded, the APP11 marker (FFEB) and segment length (Lp) of all APP11 segments containing the JUMBF data be included in the exclusion range. Notes that these APP11 segments are contiguous, so a single range is required.

States that, when hashing a PNG file into which the C2PA Manifest will be embedded, it is important to include the Length and the 'caBX' chunk type of the chunk containing the JUMBF data in the exclusion range.

Recommends that, when hashing a TIFF-based asset into which the C2PA Manifest will be embedded, the count field of the C2PA Manifest Store's IFD Entry be included in the exclusion ranges, to support Update Manifests that could change the size of the embedded C2PA Manifest Store.

Recommends that, when hashing a RIFF-based asset into which the C2PA Manifest will be embedded, the size field of the top-level RIFF chunk (the four bytes at offset 4) be included in the exclusion ranges. Explains that this supports Update Manifests, since this size field covers the whole file and is rewritten whenever the C2PA Manifest Store size changes.
Heading that opens section 16.3.2 BMFF-Based Hash; it carries no text of its own.

Requires that portions of a BMFF-based asset to be identified with a hard binding be described using BMFF-based hash assertions labelled c2pa.hash.bmff.v3. All Merkle trees used shall be balanced binary trees of minimum depth, with NULL padding only at the rightmost positions and each level more than half full. Notes that earlier versions documented c2pa.hash.bmff and c2pa.hash.bmff.v2, and requires validators to ignore any c2pa.hash.bmff assertions. The assertion shall not appear in a cloud data or external reference assertion, and the deprecated url field shall not be added by claim generators and shall be ignored by consumers.

Specifies how the BMFF hash is computed: alg selects an allowed algorithm or defaults to the Claim's alg; non-fragmented MP4 needs hash, merkle or both, fragmented MP4 validated by Merkle tree needs only merkle, and live media segments need only hash. All file bytes are hashed except boxes or subsets matching exclusions entries, with box headers following the box's inclusion or exclusion, subset offsets measured from the box start and ordered without overlap, and in v2 and v3 each non-excluded root box contributing its 8-byte big-endian absolute offset concatenated with its data (the offset omitted for Merkle hashes when both hash and merkle are present). Defines exclusion matching by xpath, length, version, flags (with exact) and data, restricts xpath to a strict abbreviated full-path subset of BMFF 4cc nodes, and requires non-leaf nodes to be plain container boxes, with the box holding an embedded manifest always excluded. Requires 'free' boxes to replace or reserve space for excluded boxes, requires post-embed offsets to be hashed, and describes three ways to achieve this: pre-inserted 'free' boxes, a two-pass approach, or placing Update Manifests at the end of the file using box_purpose values original and update.

Specifies the CDDL schema shared by the c2pa.hash.bmff.v2 (deprecated) and c2pa.hash.bmff.v3 assertions through the bmff-hash-map rule, with the complete normative schema in Section G.4.2, BMFF Hash. The map carries required exclusions plus optional alg, hash, merkle, name, deprecated url and sequenceNumber, with exclusions-map entries defined by xpath and optional length, data, subset, version, flags and exact, and merkle-map entries carrying uniqueId, localId, count, optional alg and initHash, hashes, and optional fixedBlockSize or variableBlockSizes for piecewise mdat validation. Gives CBOR diagnostic examples for a monolithic MP4, for fragmented MP4 files and for non-fragmented MP4 with a Merkle tree, plus pseudo-code for computing the BMFF-based hash and a suggested example of hashing for the Merkle map.
Heading that opens section 16.3.2.4 Exclusion list profiles; it carries no text of its own.
States that this section describes a set of pre-defined, named profiles of extension lists.
States that typical untimed media such as still photos and timed media such as videos, fragmented or not, need only include the mandatory exclusions listed in the Exclusion List Requirements.
Introduces Figure 15, Fragmented BMFF Entity Diagram, which shows the relationships among the C2PA objects that make up a fragmented BMFF manifest.

Describes validating a chunk of fragmented BMFF content: first validate the merkle-map initHash over the corresponding initialization segment, then locate the matching entry in the merkle-map hashes array and check it against the chunk's data hash, deriving it if needed with the Merkle proof from the chunk's bmff-merkle-map. Explains with Figure 16 that the c2pa-specific manifest box in each track's initialization segment contains the Manifest Store, which must be identical across multiple initialization segments, and that the active manifest's c2pa.hash.bmff.v3 assertion holds a merkle array with one merkle-map per track.

Lists the steps to verify an example chunk m+3: use the uniqueId and localId from the chunk's bmff-merkle-map to find the matching merkle-map in the init segment's c2pa.hash.bmff.v3 assertion, and verify the init segment by comparing its hash (using the assertion's exclusions and the merkle-map alg) to initHash. Then hash the chunk to derive D0,2, combine it with the proof hashes D0,3 and D1,0 from the chunk's bmff-merkle-map to derive D2,0, and treat the chunk as verified if the derived D2,0 equals the stored D2,0 in the merkle-map hashes and the initialization segment was verified.
Heading that opens section 16.3.3 General Box Hash; it carries no text of its own.

Recommends that claim generators use a general box hash assertion, labelled c2pa.hash.boxes, as a hard binding for non-BMFF box formats such as JPEG 1, PNG or GIF; it is an array of structures each listing one or more boxes and a hash over them (including any data between them). Boxes shall appear in asset order, including the C2PA Manifest box, and unlisted or out-of-order boxes cause rejection during validation. Describes the excluded flag (letting validators ignore a whole box, with an accurate hash or the single byte 00 recommended) and the exclusions byte ranges (with boxIndex, ordered, non-overlapping, confined to one box and to manifest or metadata content), where excluded set to true takes precedence over exclusions. Requires each instance of repeated box types to be listed separately, defines alg fallback from box-hash-map to box-map to Claim, and requires the C2PA Manifest Store box to be listed alone with name C2PA and hash 00 as a single box even when split across JPEG APP11 segments. The optional pad and pad2 shall be zero-filled, and the assertion shall not appear in a Cloud Data or External Reference assertion.

Defines a logical box labelled c2pa.after for multi-part formats where part data follows the primary part's box-based data; if present it shall be listed last and its hash shall cover from the byte after the last box to the end of the physical file. Requires that only the whole-asset hard binding assertion may include a c2pa.after box, while a hash assertion for an individual part shall cover only that part.
Heading that opens section 16.3.3.3 Handling for specific formats; it carries no text of its own.

Specifies JPEG 1 handling for general box hash: non-C2PA APP11 boxes shall be included in the hashed boxes, APP11 boxes holding the C2PA Manifest Store shall be identified as C2PA, and all other boxes shall use the symbols from ISO 10918-1:1994, Table B.1. Notes that the manifest store is recognizable as a JUMBF superbox labelled c2pa with the given type UUID, and that SOS and RST[n] boxes include their following entropy-coded segments. Explains that CIPA Multi-Picture Format files can be supported by listing all boxes of each Individual Image in sequence, but that if the file is treated as a multi-part asset the c2pa.after box shall be used for parts after the first image's EOI.

Explains that a PNG file always begins with an 8-byte header, and that to include it the special value PNGh is used as the first box in the list, with hashing starting from the first byte of the image.

Notes that general box hash support for TIFF, documented in previous versions, has been removed in favor of the data hash because TIFF's indirection and structure make box hashing awkward, inefficient and prone to interoperability issues.

Specifies GIF handling for general box hash: hashing a box with a Packed Fields attribute also hashes the optional data it indicates, such as Local or Global Color Tables. Requires boxes with a block label to be named "<Block Label>" and extension blocks to be named "<Extension Introducer><Extension Label>", with the header named "GIF89a", Table Based Image Data "TBID" and the Logical Screen Descriptor "LSD", and gives examples such as "3B" for the trailer and "21FE" for a Comment Extension.

Describes the nested RIFF chunk structure of L0 RIFF chunks, L1 sub-chunks and LIST chunks that nest further chunks, and specifies how they map to general box hash boxes. Each L0 chunk shall be a 12-byte box named by its media type identifier, each non-LIST L1 chunk a box named by its chunk identifier, and each LIST L1 chunk a box named by its list type identifier, with L1 boxes spanning from byte 0 through any padding byte. All L2 and deeper chunks shall be hashed as part of their LIST L1 chunk, and padding bytes shall be treated as part of, and hashed with, the preceding chunk.

Specifies that font tables, including the C2PA table, correspond directly to hash boxes enumerated in table directory order, with the table directory itself not hashed and checkSumAdjustment treated as zero when hashing the box containing the head table. Leaves the grouping of tables into boxes to the claim generator, noting that one table per box helps hashes survive re-packaging while combined boxes may not validate after a format transformation. States that, because font consumers shall not react to unrecognized tables, existing infrastructure expects the head table's checkSumAdjustment to incorporate the final content of the C2PA table.

Specifies that, for hashing an Ogg file, each logical bitstream is treated as a single box comprising all its Pages in order, with the C2PA Manifest Store box being the bitstream identified in Section A.3.7, Embedding manifests into OGG Vorbis. Requires each non-C2PA bitstream's box name to be Stream-[bitstream_serial_number], using the ASCII base-10 value of the serial number read as a 32-bit little-endian unsigned integer, so that serial number \x01\x00\x00\x00 yields "Stream-1".

Specifies the CDDL schema for the general box hash through the box-map rule (boxes and optional alg) and box-hash-map (names, optional alg, hash, optional excluded, exclusions, pad and pad2), with box-exclusions-map entries of start, length and optional boxIndex, and refers to Section G.4.4, Boxes Hash, for the complete normative schema. Gives CBOR diagnostic examples for JPEG 1, PNG, GIF, TTF and JXL. Requires exclusion start and length values to use preferred (shortest) serialization normally, but to be written as 32-bit integers when not yet known.
Heading that opens section 16.3.4 Collection Data Hash; it carries no text of its own.

Requires that, when a C2PA Manifest is known in advance to refer to a collection of assets rather than a single asset, the collection data hash assertion be used to specify the hard bindings for the assets in the collection. Notes that each folder of an AI/ML training data set can be described as a separate ingredient of the full data set's manifest. The assertion shall be labelled c2pa.hash.collection.data and shall not appear in a cloud data assertion.

Specifies the CDDL schema for the collection data hash assertion through the collection-data-hash-map rule, which holds a uris array of hashed URI entries, a required alg and an optional zip_central_directory_hash, and also allows URN-based record identifiers per RFC 8141; the complete normative schema is in Section G.4.5, Collection Data Hash. Gives CBOR diagnostic examples for a list of remote URLs, a list of relative file URIs and relative paths inside an EPUB.

Defines the collection data hash fields: uris is an array of uri-hashed-data-map values representing the collection, and alg, if present, shall name an allowed hash algorithm used for every member, otherwise the Claim's alg applies. Each entry shall have a uri that is a valid relative URI resolved against the manifest's location (except for container formats whose members use a native absolute URI, such as a WARC-Record-ID, where the uri shall be that identifier), and claim generators shall validate or sanitize URIs so that neither . nor .. appear. The uri shall not contain a query component, though a fragment is permitted, because it names a static hashed content item. The hash field holds the hash over all bytes of the content item with no exceptions, and the remaining fields are identical to those of an ingredient assertion.

Requires each file in the collection to be hashed individually with the algorithm in the alg field, with the result stored in the hash field of the uri-hashed-data-map for that file's uri. States that not every file in a hierarchy needs to be included, noting that this also gives an adversary an opening to add files without invalidating the binding.
