Heading that opens section 16.3.5 Multi-Asset Hash; it carries no text of its own.

Describes file formats composed of multiple parts that are each valid files, such as CIPA Multi-Picture Format, Android Ultra HDR, ISO 21496 HDR and Android Motion Photo. Explains that existing hard binding assertions cannot separately verify each part's integrity or record parts' own C2PA Manifests, and that the multi-asset hash assertion provides this. Also notes the case of an optional part that may be removed by a workflow without a trusted signer while the rest of the file remains verifiable.

Requires the multi-asset hash assertion to be labelled c2pa.hash.multi-asset; although it contains hashes and modifies hard binding handling, it is not considered a hard binding, it shall not appear in a cloud data or external reference assertion, and it should not be used with a compressed manifest. Every part, including the primary part, shall be a part-hash-map in the parts array, listed in file order, contiguous, non-overlapping and covering every byte, with a location locator giving either byteOffset and length or a bmffBox whose payload (excluding header) is the part. The hashAssertion field shall be a hashed URI to a standard hard binding assertion whose label has .part and any multiple instance identifier appended (e.g. c2pa.hash.data.part__2), with absolute offsets computed relative to the part's start. The optional boolean field defaults to false, and a part's own C2PA Manifest that is not self-contained is recommended to be stored in the asset's Manifest Store and referenced through a componentOf ingredient.

Specifies the CDDL schema for the multi-asset hash assertion through the multi-asset-hash-map rule, whose parts array holds part-hash-map entries with a location (either a byte range or a bmffBox), a hashAssertion hashed URI and an optional optional flag; the full normative schema is in Section G.4.6, Multi-Asset Hash. Gives a CBOR diagnostic example of a two-part 33,333-byte asset with c2pa.hash.boxes.part and c2pa.hash.data.part assertions for the parts and an overall c2pa.hash.boxes assertion using c2pa.after, and illustrates its use for an HDR gain map in Figure 17.
Heading that opens section 16.3.6 Segment Hash; it carries no text of its own.

Describes the problem of append-only files such as application logs, event logs and JSON Lines streams, where a single hard binding over the whole file would be invalidated by the next line written. Explains that a segment hash assertion binds a manifest to one bounded segment, the bytes added since the previous checkpoint, and records the position and length of the sentinel line carrying its manifest plus a digest of the preceding checkpoint's sentinel line so history cannot be rewritten without breaking the chain. Refers to Section A.3.17, Embedding manifests into append-only text files, for how checkpoints are written.

Requires the segment hash assertion to be labelled c2pa.hash.segment; it is a hard binding to be used only for assets described in Section A.3.17, and it shall not appear in a cloud data or external reference assertion. The version field shall be 1, alg (if present) shall name an allowed algorithm used for both hash and predecessorSentinel.hash (else the Claim's alg), segmentStart and segmentEnd mark the segment up to the start of the sentinel line (segmentStart being 0 for the first checkpoint), and hash covers [segmentStart, segmentEnd). The sentinelLength field shall be present when the sentinel line references the manifest store by external URI and absent when it embeds it inline, because the inline length cannot be known at signing time. The predecessorSentinel field shall be present for every checkpoint after the first, locating and hashing the preceding sentinel line, and absent for the first.

Specifies the CDDL schema for the segment hash assertion through the segment-hash-map rule, with version 1, optional alg, hash, segmentStart, segmentEnd, optional sentinelLength, optional predecessorSentinel and optional metadata, and a predecessor-sentinel-map whose start, length and hash fields are required together; the full normative schema is in Section G.4.7, Segment Hash. Gives a CBOR diagnostic example using the offsets and hashes of the second checkpoint from Section A.3.17.6, Test vectors.
Heading that opens section 16.3.7 Soft Binding; it carries no text of its own.

Requires that a soft binding a claim generator provides for an asset's content be described using a soft binding assertion labelled c2pa.soft-binding. Deprecates the never-used url field in favor of the asset reference assertion, so claim generators shall not add it and consumers shall ignore it. Also deprecates the extent field within scope in favor of the region field, so claim generators shall not add it and consumers should ignore it; in both cases the field still counts as part of the content validated per Section 14.10.4, Assertion Validation.

Specifies the CDDL schema for the soft binding assertion through the soft-binding-map rule, with alg, blocks, optional pad, pad2, name, alg-params, bindingMetadata, deprecated url and metadata; each soft-binding-block-map has a scope (deprecated extent, timespan in milliseconds or region) and a value, and the full normative schema is in Section G.5.12, Soft Binding. Gives a CBOR diagnostic example using the phash algorithm with two timespan blocks.

Requires the soft binding algorithm to be given in the alg field and the blocks it was applied over to be listed in blocks, and recommends that any extra algorithm parameters be placed in alg-params. Allows the scope field to contain either a region (a region-map from Section 16.9.2, Regions of Interest) or a timespan in milliseconds from the start of the content, and requires pad and pad2, if present, to be zero-filled byte strings.

Allows a soft binding assertion to include a bindingMetadata key carrying pre-defined and custom algorithm- or workflow-specific fields, with custom fields required to follow entity-specific namespacing (e.g. com.litware.someFieldName). States that a C2PA Validator should not use this information when validating the soft binding but may use it for logging or informational purposes, since the normative validation information is in the other assertion fields and the algorithm's entry in the Soft Binding Algorithm List.

Describes the soft binding algorithm list, a machine-readable JSON document maintained by the C2PA at https://sbal.c2pa.org, as the list of recommended values for the alg field, which should match an entry's alg. Entries marked deprecated shall not be used to create soft binding assertions, and resolving with them is discouraged; validators should not resolve such bindings. Gives the JSON schema for entries and requires each entry's alg to follow namespacing and represent the owner, each algorithm version to have its own entry, type to be watermark or fingerprint, and supported media types to be given as encodedMediaTypes or decodedMediaTypes based on IANA types. Requires entryMetadata with a description and dateEntered, a required contact email and a required informationalUrl to a page describing the algorithm, including the algorithm-specific format of alg-params and value.

Describes the soft binding resolution API as a Web API for retrieving C2PA Manifest stores from an endpoint given a soft binding value, a manifest identifier or an asset. States that a soft binding algorithm list entry may list resolution API URIs in softBindingResolutionApis, any of which may be used, and points to the separate API specification.

Describes using soft bindings to discover the active manifest in a manifest repository for an asset whose C2PA Manifest is absent or invalid, requiring discovery to use one or more algorithms identified in the C2PA Soft Binding Algorithm List. Requires that, if the located manifest contains soft binding assertions, the matcher ensure all of them match the soft bindings used for discovery. A soft binding assertion matches when both its alg and value match those used, with matching performed as the specified algorithm prescribes.
Describes the provenance and workflow assertions as those recording how an asset came to be, namely the actions performed on it and its relationships to other assets and external resources.
Heading that opens section 16.4.1 Actions; it carries no text of its own.

Describes the actions assertion as an array of actions on the asset's content, each stating what happened and optionally when and with what software, with array order unspecified except as noted in Section 16.4.1.2. Distinguishes the deprecated v1 (c2pa.actions) from v2, which shall be labelled c2pa.actions.v2 and may derive actions from a templates array, and notes that actions are modelled after XMP ResourceEvents. Requires each action value to be a pre-defined or entity-specific action name. Lists the pre-defined c2pa. actions in Table 4 with their meanings and whether each is a perceptible or non-editorial transformation (for example c2pa.created, c2pa.opened, c2pa.edited, c2pa.modified, c2pa.redacted, c2pa.watermarked.bound, with c2pa.color_adjustments, c2pa.removed and c2pa.watermarked deprecated), noting that perceptible means an action can produce a perceptible change, and lists the font. actions in Table 5, which replace the deprecated c2pa.font prefix.

Requires at least one actions assertion in the created_assertions of a standard C2PA Manifest's Claim. For an asset created de novo the first c2pa.actions assertion shall begin with a c2pa.created action carrying an appropriate digitalSourceType (http://c2pa.org/digitalsourcetype/empty when there is no digital content); for an asset created by opening an existing asset as a parentOf ingredient it shall begin with c2pa.opened, with a matching c2pa.ingredient.v3 assertion referenced in the action's parameters ingredients. Notes that this does not apply to Update Manifests and that c2pa.opened needs no digitalSourceType, and requires that a manifest's actions contain no more than one c2pa.created or c2pa.opened action. Gives examples of a generative AI video, an image built from a template with placed photos, and a newsroom edit of a camera-captured photo.

Requires the claim generator to set the allActionsIncluded boolean in actions-map-v2, where true states that all actions performed are described and false states that unrecorded actions may have occurred; manifest consumers should interpret an omitted field as indicating that unrecorded actions may have been performed, and the field was optional in previous versions. Requires allActionsIncluded to be true when an asset is opened only to record c2pa.opened and immediately re-saved without other changes. Notes that external reference assertions with a hashed location can provide bound data about a process and be linked to actions via relatedAssertions.
Heading that opens section 16.4.1.4 Fields in the actions assertion; it carries no text of its own.

Allows an action to include a free-text description field explaining what the action does, most useful for non-standard actions but also usable to add information to a standard action, such as "Paintbrush tool" for c2pa.edited.

Requires that the reason field, if present, contain one of the standard values c2pa.PII.present, c2pa.invalid.data, c2pa.trade-secret.present or c2pa.government.confidential, or a custom value following entity-specific namespacing. Notes that only redaction-focused c2pa values are defined so far, and requires that a c2pa.redacted action's reason field contain the rationale for the redaction.

Allows an action to include a when field for the time of the action, which shall be a CBOR date/time and shall be interpreted as whenStart and whenEnd sharing the same absolute value; claim generators should use when for a single exact time. A v2 action may instead use whenStart (generator-lower-bound-time-type) and whenEnd (generator-upper-bound-time-type) as defined in Section 8.9, with whenStart not later than whenEnd when both are present, and when shall not appear together with either of them. Notes that these are claim-generator-provided timestamps and that UTC-based times should be used.

Describes the softwareAgent field identifying the software or hardware that performed an action, a text string in v1 and a generator-info-map in v2. When multiple softwareAgents are used, softwareAgentIndex shall reference the agent by its 0-based index in the softwareAgents array, and an action shall have only one of softwareAgent or softwareAgentIndex. Notes that these fields help when the agent differs from the claim generator and that the earlier actors field was removed in version 2.0.

Allows an action to include a digitalSourceType whose value shall be an IPTC-defined term or one of the C2PA values http://c2pa.org/digitalsourcetype/empty (effectively empty content) or http://c2pa.org/digitalsourcetype/trainedAlgorithmicData (model-derived data in a data format rather than a media type). Notes its common use with c2pa.created to indicate how media was created, and states that for trained algorithmic assets one or more ingredients may be added to describe the inputs and referenced from a c2pa.placed or c2pa.created action.

Describes how to identify a specific action instance, either implicitly or explicitly. Recommends implicitly using the JUMBF URI of the actions assertion and, for a specific action, appending &cbor= with a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) path such as /actions/1, observing all JSON Pointer rules. Suggests a custom parameters key such as com.fabrikam.actionId for an explicit identifier.

Explains that an action may apply to only part of an asset, such as a range of video frames or an image area; in v1 this was a text string, while in v2 it is a changes field holding an array of region-map objects from Section 16.9.2, Regions of Interest.

Describes the parameters key for action-specific pre-defined and custom fields, with custom fields required to follow entity-specific namespacing, and the optional multipleInstances field, whose absence means it is unknown whether the action was repeated. Requires c2pa.opened and c2pa.placed actions to hold hashed JUMBF URIs to related ingredient assertions in ingredient (v1) or ingredients (v2), allows a c2pa.deleted action to reference a componentOf ingredient whose content it fully removes, and recommends regionOfInterest metadata when only part of an ingredient is relevant. Requires sourceLanguage and targetLanguage in c2pa.translated to be BCP 47 codes and the redacted field of c2pa.redacted to hold the JUMBF URI of the redacted assertion, and allows an optional machine-readable name field that sub-classifies the action. Gives an example c2pa.created action for a Generative AI image referencing two ingredients.

Allows an action's parameters to include relatedAssertions, an array of one or more hashed JUMBF URIs to related assertions in the same C2PA Manifest. Entries shall not reference actions or ingredient assertions (c2pa.actions, c2pa.actions.v2, c2pa.ingredient, c2pa.ingredient.v2 or c2pa.ingredient.v3), and Manifest Consumers may use them to present additional context. Notes that this lets an action reference, for example, an assertion metadata assertion.

Requires that a c2pa.watermarked.bound action be accompanied by a soft binding assertion describing the inserted watermark, which the action should reference through relatedAssertions in its parameters. Notes that c2pa.watermarked is deprecated in favor of c2pa.watermarked.bound and c2pa.watermarked.unbound.
Heading that opens section 16.4.1.6 Action Templates; it carries no text of its own.

Describes v2 action templates, which a C2PA Manifest Consumer combines with actions of the same name, or with all actions when the template's action is *, merging multiple applicable templates starting with * and then in array order. Requires the consumer to take template values and overlay the action's own values, replacing any with the same name, and illustrates this with examples and Figure 18, Actions Template Flow. Template parameters are merged key by key with the action's parameters, the action's values taking precedence, or used unchanged if the action has none. The templateParameters key is deprecated in favor of parameters, and consumers shall treat its pairs as parameters using the same precedence rules.

Describes the softwareAgents field, an array of generator-info-map objects that can list multiple software or hardware agents, each referenced by index through the softwareAgentIndex field of an action or template. Gives a CBOR diagnostic example of six actions referencing two agents.

Allows a template to include an icon, a raster or vector image the Manifest Consumer can use to represent the action, but requires icons to appear only in templates for entity-specific actions. The icon value, if present, shall be a hashed URI to an embedded data assertion (labelled c2pa.icon and following the multiple-instance label rules) or a cloud data assertion, matching the structure of the icon field in the Claim's Generator Info Map. Recommends that Manifest Consumers also support the data box approach from earlier versions.
Requires that, if an actions assertion's metadata contains a localization dictionary for a template, those localizations also apply to every action based on that template.

Describes the v2 related field for listing additional actions related to a primary action, usually occurring at the same time. Recommends that each related action include only the fields that differ from the primary action, with a C2PA Manifest Consumer merging the values with the primary action, as with a template, to get the full picture.

Describes using the actions assertion to signal a claim creator's intent when creating asset renditions for different connectivity, resolution and other environments. The presence of only c2pa.published, c2pa.transcoded and c2pa.repackaged actions signals that the signer asserts no editorial changes to the digital content occurred between the ingredient(s) and this asset, and a single parentOf ingredient further signals that the asset was derived directly from that parent.

Allows a claim generator performing c2pa.opened or c2pa.placed with an asset lacking a C2PA Manifest to use a soft binding lookup to find its manifest, and recommends adding any located manifest as the ingredient assertion's activeManifest. If it does so, the ingredient assertion shall also contain softBindingsMatched set to true and a softBindingAlgorithmsMatched array with at least one entry, indicating to consumers that a lookup was used. Notes that validation failures are to be expected in the ingredient assertion because recovered manifests usually carry non-matching hard bindings, and gives a CBOR diagnostic example.

Allows a claim generator to use a c2pa.deleted action when a deletion removes all the content of an ingredient previously recorded with a componentOf relationship, indicating it should no longer be considered part of the asset. If that ingredient assertion is also redacted, a c2pa.redacted action should be used as well and the c2pa.deleted action should reference the redacted ingredient assertion.

Summarises the requirements that link actions assertions, which record what happened to an asset, with ingredient assertions, which record the other assets or data involved, noting that adding one often requires a matching entry in the other and that c2pa.opened and c2pa.placed actions must reference their ingredient assertions. It gives further examples: a c2pa.created action may reference inputTo ingredients such as Generative AI inputs, and a c2pa.deleted action may reference a componentOf ingredient and should be paired with c2pa.redacted when that ingredient assertion is also redacted.

Explains that an ingredient's digitalSourceType can be inferred from its active manifest if it has one, or otherwise carried in the ingredient assertion itself, that an ingredient assertion shall not contain both activeManifest and digitalSourceType, and that an ingredient may declare no digitalSourceType at all.

Lists eight deprecated actions (c2pa.copied, c2pa.formatted, c2pa.version_updated, c2pa.printed, c2pa.managed, c2pa.produced, c2pa.saved and c2pa.removed), which shall no longer be written into c2pa.actions or c2pa.actions.v2 assertions but may appear in pre-existing manifests.

Gives the CDDL schemas for the actions assertions, with c2pa.actions defined by the deprecated actions-map rule and c2pa.actions.v2 by actions-map-v2, plus the generated list of predefined action names (c2pa.* and font.* actions, with a pattern allowing custom names). The v2 schema defines a required actions array and allActionsIncluded flag, optional templates, softwareAgents and metadata, and per-action fields such as softwareAgent, description, digitalSourceType, exact or ranged timing (when, or whenStart and whenEnd), changes, related, reason (required for c2pa.redacted) and parameters including redacted, ingredients, relatedAssertions, sourceLanguage, targetLanguage, name and multipleInstances. It also gives a CDDL for font-specific action parameters (Unicode ranges and variable-font instance settings such as weight, width, italic, slant and optical size) and a CBOR diagnostic example of a v2 actions assertion with a filtered and a cropped action.
Heading that opens Section 16.4.2, External Reference; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

Defines the external reference assertion (label c2pa.external-reference), which points to data stored remotely, either advisory and changeable via an unhashed-ext-uri-map or cryptographically bound at signing via a hashed-ext-uri-map, in a required location field with an optional label when the target is a complete assertion; it should appear in gathered_assertions and shall not reference actions, hash, cloud-data, external-reference or ingredient assertions. Referenced data shall be treated as optional and should not be retrieved during manifest validation, unhashed retrieved data shall be treated as advisory unless independently verified, and the size field should be omitted when the referenced data may change.

States that the hashed variant of an external reference assertion may point to externally stored creation-process evidence, identified through the data_types field using the predefined values c2pa.types.audit-log and c2pa.types.version-history (or entity-specific types following namespace syntax), with processStart and processEnd in metadata describing the process where applicable.

Gives the CDDL for the external reference assertion as two rules, external-reference-map with an unhashed location and hashed-external-reference-map with a hashed location, each also allowing optional label, description and metadata fields. It also defines the unhashed-ext-uri-map (url plus optional dc:format, size and data_types) and the hashed-ext-uri-map, which additionally requires alg and hash. CBOR diagnostic examples show unhashed references to a remote c2pa.metadata assertion, an arbitrary blob and changing JSON data, and hashed references to an audit log and a version history.
Heading that opens Section 16.4.3, Linked Resource Integrity; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

Defines the linked resource integrity assertion (label c2pa.linked-resource-integrity), which provides hash coverage, akin to W3C Subresource Integrity, for external resources referenced by container formats, using a resources field holding either an externalResources array of hashed absolute URLs or a relativeResources array with a shared alg; it shall appear only in created_assertions, and relative URIs shall be resolved against the asset's location, or treated as unresolvable when that location is unknown. The optional allURIsIncluded flag, when true, says every fetched or embedded reference the signer can enumerate at signing time is covered, excluding navigational links, the manifest itself and transitively discovered resources, while an absent value should be read as meaning more references may exist; validators are not required to retrieve resources, so hash checking is optional.

Gives the CDDL for the linked resource integrity assertion, where linked-resource-integrity-map holds resources as either an external-resources-map or a relative-resources-map (with its own alg), plus optional allURIsIncluded and metadata. It also defines the hashed-ext-uri-map and the uri-hashed-data-map, whose relative URI type permits no scheme or authority and leaves rejection of percent-encoded traversal to validation. Two CBOR diagnostic examples show an HTML asset with two fully covered external resources and a MaterialX scene with one relative texture and partial coverage.
Heading that opens Section 16.4.4, Asset Reference; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

Defines the asset reference assertion (label c2pa.asset-ref), which records via URIs one or more locations, a single asset or a directory of collection-hashed assets, where a copy of the asset may be obtained, with the metadata time stamp giving a basis for judging link freshness.

Gives the CDDL for the asset reference assertion, where asset-ref-map holds a required references array whose entries pair a reference containing a uri with an optional human-readable description, plus optional metadata. A CBOR diagnostic example lists one web location and one IPFS location.
Heading that opens Section 16.4.5, Repository Receipt; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

Defines the repository receipt assertion (label c2pa.repository-receipt), which may record proof that a C2PA Manifest Repository ingested a manifest and shall appear only in an update manifest, with a body that is a JSON-LD object including @context. Its repository object shall give the repository's base uri and a canonical manifestId, and its anchor object shall give a uri where the proof can be verified and a repository-defined proof object, with optional repository-specific parameters.

Gives the JSON Schema for the repository receipt assertion payload, requiring @context, an @type fixed to org.c2pa.repository-receipt, a repository object (uri and manifestId) and an anchor object (uri and proof, with optional parameters). An example JSON object shows a receipt from a repository with an anchor URI, a view parameter and a proof value.

Introduces the ingredient assertion, which describes an asset used in creating, or otherwise related to, the asset described by the manifest, together with its relationship to that asset and a reference to its own provenance data.

Explains that ingredients record the provenance of assets composed into, derived from or rendered from other assets, and also describe assets or data used as input to processes such as AI/ML training or inference. It names three versions of the assertion, deprecated c2pa.ingredient and c2pa.ingredient.v2 and the current c2pa.ingredient.v3, which shall be the label used and addresses validating ingredients after redaction, with the usual multiple-instance labelling applying.

Specifies that an ingredient containing a C2PA Manifest takes its unique identifier from the manifest label of its active manifest, making instanceID unnecessary, while an instanceID supplied by the claim generator shall be determined as specified for non-C2PA assets, and may be supplied even when a manifest exists.

Requires each ingredient's relationship to be described as parentOf (the asset is derived from or a rendition of it, also used with update manifests), componentOf (it is one part of a composed asset) or inputTo (it was input to a computational process such as an AI/ML model). In Standard Manifests a claim generator adding an ingredient shall ensure a c2pa.actions assertion exists and add c2pa.opened for parentOf or c2pa.placed for componentOf, and a parentOf or componentOf ingredient assertion shall be listed in the same claim field (created_assertions or gathered_assertions) as the actions assertion referring to it.

Specifies that dc:title, if present, shall be a human-readable ingredient name taken from XMP or a filesystem name, but claim generators should not set it when the information is available in the ingredient's active manifest.

Specifies that dc:format, if present, shall be the ingredient's IANA media type, that claim generators should provide it with a valid value, and that multi-file ingredients such as an AI/ML data set shall use multipart/mixed.

Gives the CDDL for the ingredient assertion in its current v3 form (ingredient-map-v3) and the deprecated v2 and v1 forms, along with the format-string pattern and the relationship values parentOf, componentOf and inputTo. The v3 map requires only relationship and offers optional fields including dc:title, dc:format, validationResults, instanceID, data, dataTypes, either activeManifest or digitalSourceType but not both, relatedAssertions, claimSignature, thumbnail, description, informationalURI, softBindingsMatched, softBindingAlgorithmsMatched and metadata. A CBOR diagnostic example shows a parentOf ingredient with a thumbnail, related assertion, active manifest, claim signature and validationResults including ingredientDeltas.

Allows an ingredient to carry a free-text description field about what it is or is used for, which should be produced by the claim generator rather than contain user-provided information, user descriptions instead going in a custom assertion.
Heading that opens Section 16.5.8, Ingredient Data; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

Explains that an ingredient's own data, important for uses such as Generative AI, can be supplied through the data field, as a hashed-uri to an embedded data assertion or a hashed-ext-uri-map to external data, and that claim generators should weigh size since embedded data is carried into future manifests unless redacted. Where data can be neither embedded nor linked, such as a private AI model, an asset type in data_types can describe it, and examples show prompt, public model and private model ingredients.

Recommends that an ingredient made of multiple files, such as an AI/ML training data set, include its C2PA Manifest in the ingredient assertion and that the data set's manifest include an asset reference assertion pointing to where the files are found.

Specifies that a URL to a web page about an ingredient, such as AI/ML model details, should go in the informationalURI field, which is not an authenticated link to the ingredient's content and was named informational_URI in deprecated versions.

Specifies that a thumbnail recording an ingredient's state at import shall be added as a thumbnail assertion referenced by hashed-uri, and also added to relatedAssertions when newly created in the active manifest, while Manifest Consumers should still support the earlier data box approach.

Allows the claim generator to use the ingredient's relatedAssertions field, an array of hashed JUMBF URIs to non-ingredient, non-action assertions in the same manifest, to mark assertions that are about the ingredient rather than the current asset, though such assertions should appear in the ingredient's own manifest where possible. Each referenced assertion shall have a label ending in .ingredient (for example c2pa.ai-disclosure.ingredient or com.litware.metadata.ingredient) following the usual multiple-instance rules, and an example shows an inputTo ingredient referencing an AI disclosure assertion.
Heading that opens Section 16.5.12, Existing manifests; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

Requires the claim generator to copy every validated C2PA Manifest from an ingredient's Manifest Store that is not already in the asset's store, subject to the copying rules or user or configuration direction. It should also copy unvalidated manifests and unrecognised JUMBF boxes and superboxes, to stay compatible with custom assertions and future constructs.
Heading that opens Section 16.5.13, Copying existing manifests; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

Sets out the procedure a claim generator shall follow to decide whether to copy each manifest from an ingredient's Manifest Store: validate the ingredient (optionally stopping on failure if so directed), compare manifest URNs with those already in the asset's store, and on a URN match compare manifest box hashes, not copying when they match. When hashes differ only because of redaction it keeps the existing manifest, replaces it, or redacts it to the union of both redaction sets depending on where redactions were applied, and in all other cases it copies the ingredient's manifest, re-labelled with a new URN.

Gives two examples of manifest copying in which claim generator D imports ingredient B (carrying manifest A) and then ingredient C carrying a redacted manifest A, which D uses to overwrite its copy of A. In the second, the version of A from C fails validation, so D copies it under a new URN instead, with a note that non-manifest JUMBF boxes need not be copied.

Requires that when an ingredient's active manifest has been copied into the asset's store, hashed_uri references to its manifest box and claim signature box be stored in the ingredient assertion's activeManifest and claimSignature fields. An ingredient added without a manifest may instead carry a digitalSourceType drawn from the values allowed for actions, an ingredient assertion shall not contain both activeManifest and digitalSourceType, and an example shows a componentOf ingredient marked as trained algorithmic media.
Heading that opens Section 16.5.13.4, Ingredient validation; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

Requires the claim generator, when an ingredient assertion references a C2PA Manifest, to validate the ingredient and record all success, informational and failure codes in validationResults or validationStatus for use in future validations. A recorded failure is treated as an explicit statement that an actor knowingly chose to proceed despite errors, and claim generators are advised to raise warnings prominently.

Describes validationStatus in deprecated v2 ingredient assertions, optional and possibly empty without c2pa_manifest, and otherwise an array of status-map objects each with a code, an optional success boolean, an optional explanation and a url that should point to the failing claim, signature or assertion. Custom status codes are permitted but shall follow entity-specific namespace syntax and include a success boolean.

Requires a v3 ingredient assertion with activeManifest to carry validationResults, which may also appear without it, for example when a remote manifest could not be retrieved, and which shall hold full results for the ingredient's active manifest plus ingredientDeltas giving, for each manifest-bearing ingredient assertion in the ingredient's store, its ingredientAssertionURI and validationDeltas omitting statuses already recorded (compared on type, code and url). Each status-map shall contain a code and may contain a url and explanation, custom codes shall follow entity-specific namespace syntax, and a worked example and a manifest.inaccessible example illustrate usage. The results map may also carry a SemVer specVersion and either the deprecated trustListUri or trustListUris, whose objects shall each give the uri and type (such as c2pa.trustList or c2pa.tsaTrustList) of a trust list where a trust anchor matched, with an optional identifier that for ETSI-formatted lists shall be the list's sequence number.

Explains that an ingredient assertion's metadata field may carry information such as generation time to help Manifest Consumers judge provenance. When only part of an ingredient is used, metadata should include a regionOfInterest describing the parts used, as an example with temporal and track regions shows.

Requires that when an active manifest includes as a parentOf ingredient a manifest found through a soft binding lookup, the ingredient assertion shall set softBindingsMatched to true and list in softBindingAlgorithmsMatched the algorithm names, as identified in the C2PA Soft Binding Algorithm List, used to find it.

Introduces the content description and enrichment assertions, which carry extra information about an asset or alternative representations of its content, such as thumbnails, metadata, format-specific details and externally stored data.
Heading that opens Section 16.6.1, Thumbnail; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

States that a thumbnail assertion gives an approximate visual representation of the asset at a specific lifecycle event, of which there are two, ingredient import and claim creation, each with its own label; the extracted list appears garbled, splitting this into two bullets that do not each name an event.

Specifies that a thumbnail made at claim creation shall be labelled c2pa.thumbnail.claim, with at most one per manifest, and that the older convention of adding the media type to the label is deprecated.

Specifies that importing an ingredient should reference its own manifest-stored thumbnail, or, where none exists, a new thumbnail should be generated and stored as an ingredient thumbnail assertion whose label shall start with c2pa.thumbnail.ingredient, follow multiple-instance rules, and be added to the ingredient's relatedAssertions. It notes that earlier conventions of media-type suffixes and a _1 suffix with a single underscore for the first instance are deprecated.
States that a thumbnail assertion is an embedded data assertion distinguished by a special label for this use.
Heading that opens Section 16.6.2, Alternative Content Representation; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

Defines the alternative content representation assertion, which shall have the label c2pa.alternative-content-representation and refers to digital content different from the primary asset, with parameters that depend on the file format as specified in the following sections.
Heading that opens Section 16.6.2.2, Original Preservation Image; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

Describes using the alternative content representation assertion to reference an Exif Original Preservation Image (OPI), the unprocessed capture-time image, either where it sits in the asset's MPF, located by its index in the parts array of the multi-asset hash assertion, or moved into the manifest, as typically happens when the format changes from Exif or the file becomes an ingredient. A moved OPI shall be recorded unchanged as an embedded data assertion, edits preserving the OPI should add a new assertion, removal shall be recorded with c2pa.deleted or by redaction rules, and a manifest shall not contain more than one such assertion labelled exif.originalPreservationImage.

The schema defines the c2pa.alternative-content-representation assertion in CDDL as either an original-preservation-image-representation (type exif.originalPreservationImage, with parameters multiAssetPartIndex or embeddedOriginalPreservationImage) or a generic-representation with a namespaced type and free-form parameters. It requires the type to be exif.originalPreservationImage and the parameters to reference the original preservation image either by its part index in an MPF asset or by a hashed URI to an embedded data assertion in the manifest, but not both, with CBOR examples of each case.
Heading that opens Section 16.6.3, Asset Type; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

The asset type assertion, labelled c2pa.asset-type.v2 and limited to one per manifest, gives extra context on how to parse or process an asset beyond a single Media Type, and replaces the deprecated c2pa.asset-type assertion. Its optional dc:format field holds the IANA Media Type, and its optional types field is an array of asset-type-map entries whose type value comes from the asset type or model type tables or an entity-specific namespace, with an optional version. Table 7 lists asset type values such as c2pa.types.dataset, c2pa.types.generator and serialization formats, and Table 8 lists AI/ML model type values from c2pa.types.model.caffe to c2pa.types.model.xgboost.

The CDDL defines the asset-types map, with optional dc:format, a types array of asset-type-map entries (each a type choice plus an optional SemVer version) and optional metadata. A CBOR example describes a TensorFlow 2.11.0 model stored in the SavedModel format.

When an asset's exact type is in the IANA application or text registries it should be recorded in dc:format, and an asset type assertion may combine a Dublin Core format with a C2PA standard or custom type. Table 9 lists common dc:format values such as application/json and text/csv, IANA structured suffixes like +json are also supported, and Table 10 adds two non-IANA formats, application/x-hdf5 and application/x-7z-compressed.
Heading that opens Section 16.6.4, Font Information; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

The Font Information assertion, labelled font.info with at most one per manifest, adds basic font metadata such as name, format, creator attribution and licensing so it can be validated cryptographically.

The CDDL defines font-info-map, with required fields fullName, familyName, style, weight, postScriptName (restricted to a printable ASCII pattern), format (TrueType or OpenType) and copyrightNotice, plus optional version, versionUrl, releaseDate, copyrightHolder, copyrightYears, designers, designFoundry, sourceFoundry and identifier. Supporting rules define the allowed styles, a weight map with a class name and a value from 1 to 1000, an entity map with name and URL, and a designer map with person, foundry, contribution and start and end dates. Two CBOR examples follow, a basic one and an extended one showing the optional fields.
Heading that opens Section 16.6.5, Depthmap; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

A depthmap assertion gives a 3D description of a captured scene, either as a pre-computed depth map or as data such as stereo images from which one can be computed; its label shall start with c2pa.depthmap followed by a part naming the depth map type, and the depth data shall be captured optically rather than inferred from a single 2D image.

The GDepth depthmap assertion, labelled c2pa.depthmap.GDepth, encodes a pre-computed depth map using the GDepth format, and its data schema shall always mirror the published GDepth schema, with a note that splitting data beyond 64KB is not a concern.

The CDDL defines depthmap-gdepth-map, with GDepth fields for format (RangeInverse or RangeLinear), near and far values, MIME type and base64 depth data, plus optional units, measure type, confidence image, device manufacturer, model, software and original image width and height. A CBOR example is given, and the block states that GDepth:Format, GDepth:Near, GDepth:Far, GDepth:Mime and GDepth:Data shall be present in every GDepth assertion.
Heading that opens Section 16.6.6, Embedded Data; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

The embedded data assertion replaces the deprecated data box concept, which could not be redacted, with a standard assertion holding data in a JUMBF Embedded File box; its label shall start with c2pa.embedded-data, and some other assertions such as c2pa.thumbnail.claim are technically equivalent under their own labels.

The Embedded File Description box of an embedded data assertion shall carry an IANA media type (structured suffixes allowed) and may carry a file name, shall not set the External bit, and its Binary Data box shall hold file bytes matching that media type.
Heading that opens Section 16.6.7, Cloud Data; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

The cloud data assertion, labelled c2pa.cloud-data, references a remotely stored C2PA assertion packaged as JUMBF (media type always application/jumbf) through a hashed URI, so the remote data must be static, and its contents shall be treated as optional and should not be fetched during manifest validation. It shall not refer to actions, hashing, ingredient or other cloud data assertions (a list of labels is given), and its size field shall give the referenced data's size while the size and dc:format fields of the hashed external URI map shall be omitted.

The CDDL defines cloud-data-map with a label, a size of at least 1, a hashed external URI location, an optional content_type and optional metadata, followed by a CBOR example pointing to a remote c2pa.metadata assertion.
Heading that opens Section 16.6.8, Metadata; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

Metadata is now represented by a category of assertions with a standardized serialization, replacing earlier per-standard assertions, so that included metadata is signed, attributable and processed consistently; these assertions may represent existing standards or private specifications.

A metadata assertion's label shall end in .metadata or .metadata.ingredient, preceded by c2pa or an entity-specific namespace (for example com.litware.metadata). Each shall hold a single JSON content box with a JSON-LD serialization that includes @context, and the recommended approach is to build an XMP Data Model representation and serialize it to JSON-LD.

The block defines the c2pa.metadata assertion for a subset of common metadata schemas and requires claim generators to include only the fields enumerated in Appendix C, while custom-labelled metadata assertions may hold any values. JSON-LD examples show the assertion for an image (Exif, TIFF, IPTC and Photoshop fields including GPS data) and for a PDF.

Although redaction removes only whole assertions, an update manifest allows partial redaction of c2pa.metadata by removing the original and adding a reduced version, which is then attributed to the update manifest's signer, for example keeping camera information while dropping location data.
Introduction to Section 16.7, saying these assertions carry information used in manifest validation, such as certificate status, trusted time-stamps and session keys.
Heading that opens Section 16.7.1, Certificate Status; the block holds no text beyond the heading.
The certificate status assertion supplies trusted certificate revocation status after the fact for manifests created offline, where OCSP information could not be obtained at signing time.
The CDDL defines the certificate status map as a single ocspVals array of one or more byte strings, with a CBOR example.

A certificate status assertion shall be labelled c2pa.certificate-status, appear at most once per manifest, and contain at least one ocspVals entry, storing the captured OCSP response in the same binary format used in the ocspVals array of the rVals header.
Heading that opens Section 16.7.2, Time Stamps; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

The time stamp assertion lets a trusted RFC 3161 time stamp be added later to a manifest created offline, before its signing certificate expires, giving proof of existence for the manifest and, for the active manifest, its asset.
The CDDL defines time-stamp-map as a map from C2PA manifest URNs to time stamp byte strings, with a CBOR example.

A time stamp assertion shall be labelled c2pa.time-stamp, appear at most once per manifest, and contain at least one entry keyed by the label of the manifest being time-stamped. Each value shall be the timeStampToken from an RFC 3161 TSA response obtained in detached mode by the usual process, except that the payload is the signature field of the target manifest's COSE_Sign1_Tagged claim signature.
Heading that opens Section 16.7.3, Session Keys; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

The session keys assertion provides the keys used to sign the verifiable-segment-info-map in live media workflows based on the Verifiable Segment Info method, and is not required for workflows that rely only on the per-segment C2PA Manifest Box method.

A session keys assertion shall be labelled c2pa.session-keys, at most one per manifest, and holds a keys array whose entries contain a COSE key with a kid, minSequenceNumber, createdAt, validityPeriod and a signerBinding signature over the signer's end-entity certificate. Keys shall be used only within their validity period, and new keys supplied in a later manifest may overlap earlier ones but their minSequenceNumber shall be at least the current sequence number, supporting key rotation and preventing replay.

The CDDL defines session-keys-data as an array of one or more session-key maps, each with a COSE key, minSequenceNumber, createdAt timestamp, validityPeriod in seconds and a COSE_Sign1_Tagged signerBinding. A CBOR example shows a c2pa.session-keys assertion with two P-256 keys.

Introduction to Section 16.8, saying these assertions disclose policy-relevant characteristics of an asset, such as environmental impact and the role of generative AI or human oversight in its creation.
Heading that opens Section 16.8.1, Environmental Sustainability; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

The c2pa.environmental-sustainability assertion conveys machine-generated data on the environmental costs of creating or modifying an asset, a manifest may hold several, and their data may be aggregated, including recursively across ingredients. An action may reference one through relatedAssertions, and any such reference shall be a hashed JUMBF URI to an assertion in the same manifest. The optional energy_kwh, carbon_kgco2e (gross emissions, excluding offsets) and water_litres fields shall each hold a non-negative value in their named unit, and any measurementMethod shall be a reverse-DNS namespaced custom value.

The CDDL defines environmental-sustainability-map with optional energy_kwh, carbon_kgco2e and water_litres measurement maps (a non-negative value and optional namespaced measurementMethod), metadata and custom fields. A CBOR example gives values for all three measures, though its caption describes a TensorFlow model, which does not match the example shown.
Heading that opens Section 16.8.2, AI Disclosure; the block holds no text beyond the heading.
The AI Disclosure assertion is introduced so claim generators can provide machine-readable, verifiable AI transparency information supporting automated compliance checks.

The AI Disclosure assertion shall be labelled c2pa.ai-disclosure and shall include modelType from the model type table, any scientificDomain shall follow the arXiv taxonomy, and other optional fields shall conform to the CDDL types.

The c2pa.ai-disclosure assertion complements c2pa.actions and digitalSourceType by adding model provenance, scientific domain metadata and a human oversight level. A table shows how digitalSourceType and humanOversightLevel combine, from fully autonomous AI generation to human-validated composites, and notes the assertion is not attached for digitalCreation with no trained model.

The CDDL defines ai-model-disclosure-map with a required modelType, optional modelName, modelIdentifier, scientificDomain list and metadata, and a contentProfile holding humanOversightLevel with the values fully_autonomous, prompt_guided or human_validated; further fields are listed as pending. A CBOR example discloses a Hugging Face Transformers model, though its caption describes a TensorFlow model, which does not match the example shown.
Introduction to Section 16.9, saying the structures that follow are used by the assertions above rather than being assertions themselves.
Heading that opens Section 16.9.1, Metadata About Assertions; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

Assertion metadata provides additional information about an assertion, such as when it was generated, to help Manifest Consumers judge its provenance, and consumers are not required to read any of it.
The assertion metadata structure may include custom key/value pairs, whose keys shall use entity-specific namespaces to avoid collisions.

The CDDL defines the assertion-metadata-map with optional dateTime, reviewRatings, reference, the deprecated dataSource (which claim generators shall not include), localizations, regionOfInterest, processStart, processEnd and custom fields. Supporting rules define bounded time maps with absolute, lowerBound or upperBound types, a source-map with a type and details, a rating-map with a value from 1 to 5, a code and explanation, and localization entries, followed by a CBOR example. Assertion metadata usually sits in another assertion's metadata field but can be stored separately in an assertion labelled c2pa.assertion.metadata, for example for non-JSON or non-CBOR assertions such as thumbnails.
If present, dateTime shall be a CBOR-compliant date time string indicating when the assertion was generated.
An assertion that applies to only part of an asset, such as a range of video frames or an image area, may identify that part with a regionOfInterest field holding a region-map object.
Note stating that the dataSource field is deprecated, with a pointer to Section H.1.

The optional reviewRatings array lets a claim generator attach one or more rating objects judging the quality of an assertion, and it shall not be present when a dataSource of type humanEntry.anonymous or humanEntry.credentialed is present. Each rating shall carry an integer value from 1 (worst) to 5 (best), with an optional human-readable explanation and an optional machine-readable code, drawn either from Table 11 (such as actions.unknownActionsPerformed, ingredient.notVisible or thumbnail.primaryMismatch) or from entity-specific namespaces.

Because the reference field of an assertion metadata assertion is a standard hashed_uri, it can point to assertions, and likewise claims, in manifests other than the active one, such as a c2pa.metadata assertion in an ingredient's manifest.

The optional processStart and processEnd fields describe the time span of the overall process behind the enclosing assertion, using generator lower-bound and upper-bound time types respectively, with processStart required to be no later than processEnd; a note says these are claim-generator timestamps, not trusted ones.
Heading that opens Section 16.9.1.10, Localization; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

The general localization text explains that, so consumers can read manifest information in their own language, localization information for an assertion can be added as a dictionary in the assertion's metadata.

A localization dictionary shall be a single object whose keys map to translations indexed by language in the JSON-LD style, with dot notation used for nested keys and [n] array indexing for array elements, as shown in examples translating dc:title and actions[0].softwareAgent. Third-party keys and values must be namespaced (for example com.litware), and claim generators should supply their human-readable strings this way, as in an example localizing custom actions in a c2pa.actions assertion's metadata.
Heading that opens Section 16.9.2, Regions of Interest; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

The description explains that some assertions, such as an actions assertion, apply only to part of an asset, and that a region definition is used to describe that temporal, spatial, textual or combined portion.

The central part of a region is its range field, which may describe temporal, spatial, frame or textual ranges or a combination, though a note says how consumers use combinations is not yet defined. A region may also carry the common fields name, identifier, type (from a controlled vocabulary such as IPTC's or an entity-specific value) and description, while the older role field is deprecated and shall no longer be generated.
Every range has a type of spatial, temporal, frame, textual or identified, and shall contain the matching data object: shape, time, frame, text or item.
Spatial ranges use a shape object that can represent a rectangle, circle or polygon, modelled on the IPTC Region Boundary Structure.

Temporal ranges use a time object running from a start to an end, expressed either as Normal Play Time (npt) relative to the start of the media or as absolute wall-clock time in RFC 3339 format, with npt the default and missing start or end values meaning the beginning or end of the asset; starts are inclusive and ends exclusive unless endInclusivity is set to inclusive. For wallClock ranges the end shall not precede the start and at least one shall be given, with the missing bound derived from the asset duration or, if unknown as in live streams, left open, and implementations should use minimal decimal precision and snap to the nearest earlier sample or frame where alignment matters.

A frame object defines an inclusive range of zero-based frames or pages, defaulting to the whole asset when start or end are absent, and while often used for document pages it may serve other media, though temporal ranges are recommended for time-based media where possible.

A text object defines a range using one or more W3C Web Annotation fragment identifiers, optionally refined by inclusive start and end character offsets that default to the whole fragment. A text-selector-range-map pairs a selector with an optional end selector to form a contiguous range, and multiple pairs can describe a non-contiguous range.

An item object identifies a track, media item or other discrete content item in the asset's container, using an identifier that should follow the container's naming scheme (track_id for MP4, item_ID for HEIF) and a value, so that for example track 2 of an MP4 could be singled out. Identified ranges can also name a region by a semantic value from an ontology such as the Foundational Model of Anatomy, in which case the identifier shall be the URL or URI of that schema.

The block gives the CDDL schema for the region-map rule, pointing to Section G.5.10 for the complete normative version. It defines region-map with a required array of range-map entries plus optional name, identifier, type, deprecated role, description and metadata, and range-map with a type choice of spatial, temporal, frame, textual or identified and the corresponding shape, time, frame, text or item objects. Supporting rules define shape-map (rectangle, circle or polygon in pixel or percent units with origin, size, inside and vertices), npt and wallClock time maps with regex-constrained start and end and endInclusivity, frame-map, the text selector maps, and item-map with identifier and value.

The block gives a series of region examples in CBOR diagnostic notation. They cover a combined temporal and spatial range in a video, textual ranges in DOCX, tagged and untagged PDF, Excel cells and table cells, a frame range for deleted PDF pages, a specific video track via an identified range, and an anatomy-based identified range spanning the whole asset.

The patent policy states that the C2PA follows the W3C Patent Policy (2004), with each Working Group Participant committing to license its Essential Claims in Approved Deliverables on W3C royalty-free terms, while source code is covered by the Working Group charter licence. Before a draft is approved a participant may exclude Essential Claims by written Exclusion Notice to the chair, identifying the patents or applications concerned, with any claims not listed remaining under the commitment and the chair publishing the notices.
Heading that opens Appendix A, Embedding manifests; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

The supported formats section says a C2PA Manifest is embedded as part of the asset's C2PA Manifest Store, whose location depends on the asset's format. It provides an alphabetical table mapping each well-known format, from append-only text files, AVI and DNG through JPEG, MP4, PDF, PNG, SVG, TTML, WARC, WebP and WebVTT, to its IANA media type, normative reference and the specification section that defines its embedding. Notes say native FLAC is under consideration and explain that a dash means no registered IANA media type or no cited normative reference.

For a multi-part asset, a C2PA Manifest Store shall be embedded in the primary part, containing the active manifest, whose multi-asset hash assertion shall give the location and hash of each part and should describe the provenance of the whole, while other parts may carry their own stores.
Heading that opens Section A.3, Embedding manifests into non-BMFF-based assets; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

In JPEG 1 the C2PA Manifest Store shall be carried in APP11 marker segments, written as multiple sequential, contiguous segments when it exceeds the 64K segment limit, with the same method applied to Exif compressed files and, for CIPA Multi-Picture Format assets, to the APP11 segment of the first image.
In PNG the C2PA Manifest Store shall be embedded in an ancillary, private, not-safe-to-copy chunk of type caBX that precedes the IDAT chunks.

For SVG, the binary C2PA Manifest Store must be Base64-encoded, though an external manifest is preferred. When embedded it shall be the value of a c2pa:manifest element inside the SVG metadata element, and an xmlns:c2pa namespace declaration should be added to the svg element, as an example shows.

For standalone TTML files (application/ttml+xml) the C2PA Manifest Store shall be Base64-encoded in a c2pa:manifest element at /tt:tt/tt:head/tt:metadata/c2pa:manifest with the c2pa namespace declared on the root element, whereas TTML carried inside a BMFF container uses the BMFF embedding instead, and an external manifest is preferred where toolchains drop foreign-namespace elements. Implementations shall not treat this element as a conformance error even in constrained profiles such as IMSC or EBU-TT-D, and the claim generator shall include a c2pa.hash.data assertion whose single exclusion range covers the c2pa:manifest element from opening to closing tag.

In ID3v2-compatible audio files such as MP3 or FLAC, the C2PA Manifest Store shall be embedded as the encapsulated data of a General Encapsulated Object (GEOB) whose MIME type field is set to the JUMBF media type.

The section introduces embedding in Standard MIDI Files, describing their MThd header and MTrk track chunks and the Sequencer-Specific Meta Event (FF 7F) for application data, and notes that MIDI 2.0 Clip Files are not covered.

The C2PA Manifest Store shall be embedded as an FF 7F Sequencer-Specific Meta Event placed just before the End of Track event in a designated track (the sole track for Format 0, the last for Format 1, the first for Format 2), with its data starting with the extended manufacturer identifier 0x00 0x43 0x32 followed by the store bytes. Only one such event is allowed, with duplicates meaning no manifest is treated as located, and the inserted event shall have delta-time 0 while any non-zero delta-time from the original End of Track moves to the following FF 2F event so track duration is unchanged.

A validator shall locate the manifest store by parsing MThd for the file format, picking the designated track, scanning it to End of Track for an FF 7F event starting with 0x00 0x43 0x32 whose remaining bytes are the store, and treating the asset as having no manifest if none is found.

A claim generator shall include a c2pa.hash.data assertion whose single exclusion range covers only the C2PA Manifest Store bytes following the manufacturer identifier, while the FF 7F status bytes, length field and identifier stay inside the hash and unchanged between passes.

Writing a manifest store into a MIDI file reserves a placeholder FF 7F event before End of Track, hashes the file excluding the placeholder, signs, and then replaces the placeholder with the signed store of identical length, keeping the event's length field and its encoding unchanged.

When re-embedding a manifest store of a different size, the existing FF 7F event cannot be patched in place, so the claim generator shall remove it, reserve a new one before End of Track, recompute the designated track chunk's 4-byte length, and repeat the two-pass hash, sign and replace flow. A note explains that because offsets are recomputed each pass, update manifests need not stay at a fixed file offset, unlike TIFF.
In Ogg Vorbis the C2PA Manifest Store shall be embedded in its own logical bitstream whose first packet begins with the 5-byte identifier \x00c2pa followed by the store data.

For TIFF-based files, including Exif uncompressed, TIFF/EP, DNG and other TIFF-based RAW formats, the C2PA Manifest Store shall be embedded as the data of tag 52545 (0xCD41) with tag type 7, and the TIFF ByteOrder does not govern its endianness. There shall be only one store per asset, placed in the last IFD of the main chain (in the single main IFD or a new IFD after it, otherwise as the only entry in its IFD), and it should sit at the end of the file to support update manifests without disturbing other offsets.
In RIFF-based files such as WAV, BWF, AVI and WebP, the C2PA Manifest Store shall be embedded as the data of a chunk with identifier C2PA that is the last sub-chunk of the first RIFF header chunk.

In GIF the C2PA Manifest Store shall be split into data sub-blocks of at most 255 bytes inside a single Application Extension block with identifier C2PA_GIF, whose Application Authentication Code serves as a block version (initially 1.0). The block layout is given in full and the block shall be placed after the header and before the first image descriptor.

A JPEG XL file using the box structure shall contain at most one top-level JUMBF superbox holding the C2PA Manifest Store, not shared with other JUMBF boxes, while a bare JPEG XL codestream cannot carry an embedded manifest, as an accompanying figure illustrates.

Fonts conforming to Open Font Format or OpenType may include a C2PA table holding an embedded manifest, a remote manifest URI or both, and the block notes that the table's definition that follows is preliminary.
The C2PA font table is identified by the table tag C2PA.

The C2PA font table record, given in Table 12, supports embedded, remote or both kinds of manifest store through the fields majorVersion, minorVersion, activeManifestUriOffset, activeManifestUriLength, reserved, manifestStoreOffset and manifestStoreLength, with a NULL offset recommended when a URI or store is absent. A non-embedded manifest may be remote or on the same storage system, and a JUMBF URI reference should be valid within the store.

The section introduces the IANA-registered BlockFact container formats .facti, .facta and .factv, listing their media types and describing their layout of a fixed header, JSON metadata with format_version and media_length, a media payload and typed extension blocks.
In these formats the C2PA Manifest Store shall be stored, without extra framing, as the data of an extension block of type C2PA.

Extracting the manifest store involves reading the magic bytes and metadata length, parsing the JSON metadata for media_length, skipping the media payload, and iterating the extension blocks to find the one of type C2PA.
The c2pa.hash.data assertion shall cover the whole file with a single exclusion range spanning the C2PA block's data, beginning just after its type and length fields.

Writing follows the usual placeholder, hash, sign and same-length replace flow, only one C2PA block is allowed per file (duplicates mean no manifest is treated as located), and consumers shall ignore unrecognised extension block types.

The section introduces Apache Parquet, describing its row groups and Thrift-encoded FileMetaData footer with optional key_value_metadata and trailing length and PAR1 magic number, and notes that manifests can only be embedded in non-encrypted Parquet files.

In Parquet the C2PA Manifest Store shall be Base64-encoded and stored as the value of a single key_value_metadata entry with key c2pa:manifest in the footer's FileMetaData, with more than one such entry meaning no manifest is treated as located.
A claim generator shall include a c2pa.hash.data assertion whose single exclusion range covers only the Base64-encoded value bytes of the c2pa:manifest entry in the serialized footer.

Writing a manifest into Parquet reserves a placeholder c2pa:manifest entry, hashes the file with the placeholder excluded, signs, and replaces the value with the same-length encoded manifest, so the footer length stays valid. Since Parquet libraries usually rewrite footers wholesale, claim generators should check that their writer preserves the entry's exact byte length and the order of key_value_metadata entries.
The section introduces ONNX as a format for trained machine learning models, consisting of a Protocol Buffers-encoded ModelProto whose metadata_props field holds key/value pairs.

In ONNX the C2PA Manifest Store shall be Base64-encoded and stored as the value of a single metadata_props entry with key c2pa:manifest, with more than one such entry meaning no manifest is treated as located.

A claim generator embedding a manifest in ONNX shall include a c2pa.hash.data assertion whose single exclusion range covers the Base64-encoded value bytes of the c2pa:manifest entry in the serialized ModelProto.

For ONNX models, a two-pass procedure shall be used: reserve a c2pa:manifest entry in metadata_props for a Base64 placeholder, serialise the ModelProto and hash the file excluding the placeholder, sign, then substitute the signed manifest at the same encoded length, and claim generators should keep the value's byte offset stable between passes.
Introduces the SafeTensors format, describing its layout as an 8-byte little-endian header length, a UTF-8 JSON header with a __metadata__ object of string key/value pairs, and then raw tensor data.

In SafeTensors, the Manifest Store shall be Base64-encoded and stored under a single c2pa:manifest key in the __metadata__ object, and if more than one such key is present the asset shall be treated as having no manifests.
A claim generator embedding a manifest in a SafeTensors file shall include a c2pa.hash.data assertion with one exclusion range covering the Base64 value bytes of the c2pa:manifest entry.

For SafeTensors, a two-pass procedure shall be used: reserve a placeholder c2pa:manifest key in __metadata__, hash the whole file (length field, JSON header and tensor data) excluding the placeholder, sign, then substitute the signed manifest at the same encoded length. The 8-byte header length field should stay consistent with the real header length, being updated and the exclusion range recalculated if the manifest changes it.

Introduces the method for append-only text files, in which provenance is attached through a rolling chain of signed checkpoints, each covering a bounded segment of new content and cryptographically linked to the previous one so a validator can verify the file's full history.

The method applies only to files written by appending complete lines and never rewriting earlier bytes, namely plain-text logs (text/plain) and JSON Lines streams; CSV and TSV shall instead use an external manifest, and structured text such as source code, configuration, Markdown and YAML shall use the structured text embedding method. A file with checkpoints shall not also carry a structured text manifest block, and the two methods are told apart by the sentinel delimiters (BEGIN C2PA CHECKPOINT versus BEGIN C2PA MANIFEST).

Each checkpoint shall be exactly one sentinel line appended right after its segment, delimited by -----BEGIN C2PA CHECKPOINT----- and -----END C2PA CHECKPOINT----- in plain text or written as a JSON object with a c2pa:checkpoint member in JSONL, and holding either an external URI to the Manifest Store or an inline data:application/c2pa;base64 URI, both of which validators shall accept. A file may hold many sentinel lines, and the one at the highest byte offset is the active checkpoint.

A checkpoint shall use a c2pa.hash.segment assertion as its hard binding, not c2pa.hash.data, and an example assertion with segmentStart, segmentEnd, sentinelLength and predecessorSentinel fields is given for a CRLF file.

Each checkpoint manifest shall reference the immediately preceding checkpoint manifest as a parentOf ingredient, except the first checkpoint, and chain verification rules are deferred to the segment hash validation section.
Heading that opens Section A.3.17.5, Writing a checkpoint; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

To write a checkpoint with an external URI, the claim generator chooses the manifest URI in advance, records the segment start and end offsets, hashes the preceding sentinel line for predecessorSentinel if there is one, then appends the formatted sentinel line in a single write and records its length as sentinelLength. It then builds the c2pa.hash.segment assertion from these values and signs and stores the Manifest Store at the chosen URI, so the sentinel append is the only file write, which suits WORM and append-only storage.

The inline-form procedure records segment offsets and the predecessor sentinel hash as in the external form, but builds the c2pa.hash.segment assertion without a sentinelLength field (which shall not be present), signs the Manifest Store, and appends a sentinel embedding the Base64-encoded store in one write. Omitting sentinelLength removes the circular dependency between the manifest and the sentinel's length, keeping the procedure compatible with WORM and append-only storage.
Introduces the test vectors, which use a short plain-text file with external URI sentinels and SHA-256 hashes so implementers can reproduce the values.

Test vector for a first checkpoint over the 12-byte LF segment alpha and bravo, showing the 112-byte sentinel line and the resulting c2pa.hash.segment assertion with segmentStart 0, segmentEnd 12 and sentinelLength 112.

Test vector for a second checkpoint in a CRLF file, giving the byte ranges of the first sentinel and the 16-byte second segment and the resulting assertion values, including the predecessorSentinel start, length and hash.
Test vector for a first checkpoint with an inline manifest over the same 12 bytes, where sentinelLength is absent and the hash matches the first example.
Heading that opens Section A.4, Embedding manifests into PDFs; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

In PDFs, Manifest Stores shall be embedded as embedded file streams whose file specification has AFRelationship C2PA_Manifest and whose stream Subtype is application/c2pa, with an Identity crypt filter required in encrypted PDFs.
Heading that opens Section A.4.2, Document-level Manifests; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

For a document-level manifest, the PDF catalog shall have an AF entry referencing only the embedded file specification holding the active manifest's store, also referenced from the EmbeddedFiles name tree or a FileAttachment annotation, with the annotation route required when a certifying signature exists so DocMDP restrictions are not broken. Because incremental updates allow multiple stores, the earliest store is the initial manifest and the latest the active one, and consumers shall process all manifests in all stores as if they were one store.

When a PDF signature will also be applied, the size and location of its Contents key shall be fixed before C2PA signing and added as an exclusion in the c2pa.hash.data assertion, and the PDF signature shall cover the whole PDF including the Manifest Store.

Individual PDF objects, such as images, Form XObjects, fonts, marked content or structure elements, may carry their own Manifest Store through an AF entry referencing an embedded file specification, and such object-level manifests are recommended to be referenced from the active manifest as componentOf ingredients. The manifest shall be attached as close as possible to the object that actually stores the described data, for example the Image XObject stream or font file stream.
Holds only a figure, captioned as an example of a PDF with multiple ingredient manifests, with no explanatory text.
Heading that opens Section A.5, Embedding manifests into BMFF-based assets; the block holds no text beyond the heading.

All BMFF-based assets, timed, untimed or mixed, shall use a 'uuid' box for C2PA, chosen over a 'c2pa' box because Chromium-based browsers fail on unknown top-level boxes; supported formats include MP4, fragmented MP4, M4A, HEIF and AVIF.

Gives the box definition for the C2PA 'uuid' box (its extended type, version 0, file container, zero or more allowed) and notes that one such box holds the Manifest Store while auxiliary boxes may hold extra validation data.

Defines the syntax of ContentProvenanceBox, a 'uuid' FullBox whose header carries a box_purpose string and, for manifest or original purposes, a first_merkle_aux_offset field, with the remaining bytes forming the ContentProvenanceBoxPayload. The box_purpose values are manifest, original, update and merkle, and first_merkle_aux_offset shall give the absolute offset of the first merkle box or zero if there is none.

Boxes with box_purpose manifest, original or update carry the raw Manifest Store plus optional padding; manifest and original boxes shall follow 'ftyp' and sit before the first 'mdat' or 'moov' or next to 'moov', while an update box shall be the last top-level box, and update manifests are supported by renaming manifest to original without changing hash bindings. In fragmented MP4, each initialisation segment shall carry an identical manifest box for pull usage, while live push streams shall include it in at least one of every 10 initialisation segments.
Merkle-purpose boxes carry CBOR-encoded hashes and tree proofs for Merkle-tree based validation.

Explains that large or fragmented BMFF assets use multiple hashes so parts can be validated without downloading every 'mdat', and that Merkle trees (one per 'mdat' in non-fragmented files, one per track in fragmented ones) keep the manifest small, with the manifest storing one tree row and an auxiliary box per subset giving its leaf position and the extra hashes needed. The choice of row trades manifest size against auxiliary box size and is left to the implementation, but the BMFF Hash portion of the manifest shall include the merkle field.

For a non-fragmented asset, two or more merkle boxes shall follow the last 'mdat' when the manifest holds a non-leaf row, with leaf hashes computed over 'mdat' payload subsets sized by fixedBlockSize or variableBlockSizes. The boxes shall follow subset order, be grouped contiguously per tree, and carry location values counting up from 0.

For fMP4 split across files, one merkle box shall precede the 'moof' in each fragment file and each leaf hash covers the whole fragment file minus exclusions, while for a single flat fMP4 file a merkle box shall precede each 'moof' and each leaf hash covers that 'moof' up to the next one. Concatenating split files does not yield a compliant file, so producing both forms shall treat the first as a parentOf ingredient with a c2pa.repackaged action.
Points to the live media instructions for live fMP4 transmissions and restates that in push streaming the manifest box is required only in a portion of initialisation segments.

For auxiliary merkle boxes, box_purpose shall be merkle and the data shall be raw CBOR describing how to validate part of the asset, padded so that all such boxes for one Merkle tree in a file are a fixed size.

Because some IDs such as the 'tkhd' track_id are only locally unique, a unique ID defined at manifest creation is combined with the local ID to make a globally unique identifier. A note explains that fixed-size merkle boxes let a progressively downloading client compute the offset of the box it needs and fetch only that box.
